嘉靖三十二年進士登科錄

玉音

嘉靖三十二年三月初九日，禮部尚書兼翰林院學士臣歐陽德等於奉天門奏為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中四百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩等六十六員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光祿大夫、柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士嚴嵩〔乙丑進士〕。
榮祿大夫、少保兼太子太保、禮部尚書、東閣大學士徐階〔癸未進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Thirty-second Year of Jiajing (1553)

Imperial Pronouncement

On the ninth day of the third month of the thirty-second year of Jiajing, your servant Ouyang De, Minister of Rites and concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others submitted the following memorial at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations: “In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm, four hundred candidates have been selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we duly propose sixty-six officials as examination readers and other officiants, including Yan Song, Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Huagai Hall. The classes of metropolitan graduate status and their corresponding ranks shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially prescribed by Emperor Taizu Gao: the first class shall, by precedent, comprise three men. The first shall receive lower sixth rank, and the second and third upper seventh rank, all being granted the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors.’ Those in the second class shall receive lower seventh rank and be granted ‘metropolitan graduate status.’ Those in the third class shall receive upper eighth rank and be granted ‘status equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Examination Readers

Yan Song held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement and Pillar of State. He was Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.〕

Xu Jie held the title Grand Master for Glorious Happiness. He was Junior Guardian and concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.〕

Ouyang Bijin, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Works, was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year. Tu Qiao, Grand Master for Fostering Virtue, Senior Minister of Orthodox Governance, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year. Lu Xun, Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year. Ao Xian, Expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Instructional Service, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Proctors: Ouyang De, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, Minister of Rites, and concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year. Sun Sheng, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year. Min Rulin, Grand Master for Excellent Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Rites, was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Examination Monitoring Officials: Xing Shangjian, Gentleman for Service in the Forest of Letters and Investigating Censor for the Sichuan Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year. Dong Wei, Gentleman for Service in the Forest of Letters and Investigating Censor for the Zhejiang Circuit, was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.

Officials Receiving Examination Papers: Guo Pu, Grand Master for Consultative Service, Left Vice Supervisor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, and concurrently Reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the thirty-second year of Jiajing (1553), the tribute scholars proceeded to the imperial palace for the Palace Examination. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in court dress, standing in their assigned ranks. That day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard arranged the imperial ceremonial regalia on the vermilion steps and in the vermilion courtyard. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites respectfully carried the yellow list of successful candidates, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate and posted it outside. Once this was done, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a belt were bestowed on the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency on the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites memorialized the throne, requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Chen Jin, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Deyan; he ranked seventh in family order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the eleventh day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Ying, held an honorary office conferred for longevity; and his father was Boliang. His father's former wives were both née Lin, and his mother was née Zhuo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji, Wenyou, Dajing, Xun, Zi, Shi, E, Shi, and Hui. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Deng. He placed fifty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Dazhang, registered in a civilian household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yicheng; he ranked second in family order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather was Guang; his father, Bangyan, was Office Manager in the Ministry of Revenue; and his mother was née Cai. His mother alone was living. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Yinglu, registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yiyong; he ranked third in family order and was forty-six years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Zhang, held an honorary office conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Zi; his father, Han, was a National University student; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingqi and Yinglin; his younger brothers were Yingxi, Yingli, Yingchu, Yingzhen, Yingfu, and Yingyou. He married a woman née Zang. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

萬浩，貫江西南昌府進賢縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝孟，行二十六，年三十七，七月十九日生。曾祖和〔教授，贈南京右都察院右都御史〕，祖福〔知府，封府尹，贈南京右都察院右都御史〕，父銳，前母艾氏，母張氏。具慶下，兄潮〔都察院右副都御史〕、瀾，弟沂、濂、洛〔俱縣丞〕、淳〔官生〕、瀹、潢、浚、漢。娶吳氏。江西鄉試第二十七名，會試第一百四十一名。

劉師顏，貫湖廣武昌府興國州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字方回，行四，年三十六，十二月二十一日生。曾祖鉅，祖珽，父守敬〔七品散官〕，前母莊氏，母莊氏。慈侍下，兄師顥、師頤、師頌，弟師頗。娶董氏。湖廣鄉試第七十四名，會試第四十七名。

陳綰，貫浙江紹興府上虞縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字用章，行二十，年三十四，七月二十九日生。曾祖霈，祖頊，父述〔封監察御史〕，母嚴氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄緒、紹〔知府〕、維、絳〔工部主事〕。娶陶氏。浙江鄉試第三十九名，會試第三十七名。
translation_en:
Second Class: 105 men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Wan Hao, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rumeng; he ranked twenty-sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-seven sui, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather He was a prefectural school instructor, posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief of the Nanjing Censorate (the text reads “Nanjing Right Censorate” [?]); his grandfather Fu was a prefect, granted the honorary title of prefect of a capital prefecture and posthumously granted the same censorial title. His father was Rui; his father's former wife was née Ai, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chao, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and Lan; his younger brothers were Yi, Lian, and Luo, all county vice magistrates; Chun, a student admitted by virtue of an official relative's status; and Yue, Huang, Jun, and Han. His wife was née Wu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shiyan, registered in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Fanghui; he ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-six sui, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather was Ting, and his father was Shoujing, a prestige official of the seventh rank. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Zhuang. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Shihao, Shiyi, and Shisong, and his younger brother was Shipo. His wife was née Dong. He placed seventy-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wan, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongzhang; he ranked twentieth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pei, his grandfather was Xu, and his father was Shu, granted the honorary title of Investigating Censor. His mother, née Yan, was granted the title of Lady of the Seventh Rank. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xu; Shao, a prefect; Wei; and Jiang, a secretary in the Ministry of Works. His wife was née Tao. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

秦宗道〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字仲學，行十三，年三十八，正月二十二日生〕。曾祖輝〔贈通議大夫都察院右副都御史〕，祖坤〔贈通議大夫都察院右副都御史〕，父鉞〔通議大夫都察院右副都御史〕，母陳氏〔封淑人〕。慈侍下，兄淮、宗儒〔兵馬指揮〕、汀、津，弟漢、濬、尚忠、尚質、尚文，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第八十七名，會試第一百七十九名。

translation_en:
Pang Yuan, registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weiming; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xi, his grandfather Jin, his father Ce, and his mother Lady Wang; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chun, Yong, and Jiu, and his younger brother was Kui. He married Lady Zhong. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 23rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Hongmo, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jiwen; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Wang and grandfather Han were both Instructors; his father was Yingke and his mother Lady Ding. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Hongxun, and he married Lady Xu. He placed 16th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Zongdao, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongxue; he ranked thirteenth in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather Hui and grandfather Kun were each posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his father Yue held those titles. His mother, Lady Chen, was invested with the title Lady of Virtue. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Huai, Zongru (a Commander of a Military Police Office), Ting, and Jin; his younger brothers were Han, Jun, Shangzhong, Shangzhi, and Shangwen. He married Lady Wang. He placed 87th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Zan, registered in Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangqi; he ranked forty-third in his family and was aged twenty-five, born on the fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Kongzhang, his grandfather Mengliang, his father Lou, and his mother Lady Xu; his parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Qiu, Xuan, Pei, Zuo (a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works), Kan, and Ji. He was betrothed to Lady Zheng. He placed 43rd in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 29th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Dongxu, registered in a military household in Yishi County, Puzhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Chongjiao; he ranked second in the family and was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Tingzhang, and his father Shangde, a vice prefect. His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Pan. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother Dongbi was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Dongguan, Donglin, Dongjiao, Dongfeng, and Donglong. He married a woman née Xue. He placed ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhixiao, registered in a military household in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongxi; he ranked first in the family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Huai. His legal mother was née Li, and his birth mother was née Zhao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Zhide. He married a woman née Luo and subsequently married another woman née Luo. He placed seventy-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ruji, registered in a civilian household in Ningguo County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Deqing; he ranked sixth in the family and was aged thirty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bingqing, his grandfather Dan, and his father Wanxiang, a district magistrate. His mother was née Ge, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruqi, Rugao, and Rukui; his younger brothers were Rucong, Ruzhou, Rujun, and Ruliu. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Tingshen, registered in a civilian household in Chunhua County, Binzhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Gongshu; he ranked nineteenth in the family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ji, a subprefect; his grandfather was Jiuxiao, who held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father was Zhongfu. His mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother Tingxiu was Right Vice Commissioner in the Office of Transmission; his younger brothers were Tingwen, Tingxun, and Tingjie. He married a woman née Lü. He placed fortieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Zhun, courtesy name Ruping, was registered in a military household in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Can; his grandfather, Bohe; his father, Tingxuan; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhuo, an annual tribute student, and Fu, a County Magistrate. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Wanlu, courtesy name Weixue, was registered in a military household of the Raozhou Battalion in Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yongqing; his grandfather, Guichun, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father, Zhengying, a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; and his mother, née Qiu, granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Wanjue, and his younger brothers were Wanyou, Wanyu, and Wanzhi. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fifteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jun, courtesy name Shubing, was registered in a military household of Guide Guard in Henan and was a native of Zhenping County, Nanyang Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhao; his grandfather, Xiong; his father, Huang; his mother, née Wen; and his stepmother, née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Hao. He married a woman née Hu. He placed sixty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Rusong, courtesy name Zimao, was registered in a military household in Hongtong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the second day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gao, a Department Magistrate promoted to the rank of Grand Master for Consultation (fengyi dafu); his grandfather, Jiuqing, honorifically appointed a County Magistrate; his father, Fuchu, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Guo, granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rumei, a student of the Directorate of Education, and his younger brothers were Ruchun, Rugeng, Rugang, Rutong, and Runan. He married a woman née Han. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhuang Shiyuan, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Junpin; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yisheng; his grandfather, Jinyang, was a county magistrate; his father was Jing, and his mother was née Lin. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shili, Shiqi, Shideng, and Shizhi; his wife was née Ke. He placed fifty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Gui, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingliang; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Gai, was a prefect, advanced in prestige rank to Grand Master of the Second Rank; his grandfather was Huan; his father was Hong, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bin and Shi; his wife was née Wu. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Mu, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongwen; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Yuan, was an Academician of the Hanlin Academy, posthumously appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenyi; his grandfather, Huo (㦯) [?], was Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing; his father was Chu, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ke, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Zhi; Cheng, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort; and Ji (稷). His younger brother was Ji (嵇). His wife was née Zhou, and his subsequent wife was née Wang. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Lin, registered in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boxiang; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Sheng; his mother was née Gao, and his stepmother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi, and his younger brother was Jiu (麔); his wife was née Li. He placed forty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

何寵〔貫浙江台州府臨海縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝錫，行一，年四十二，八月十一日生〕。曾祖允直，祖侃，父從良〔典史〕，母汪氏。慈侍下，弟寬〔南京刑部主事〕、寀，娶顧氏。浙江鄉試第十五名，會試第五十六名。
translation_en:
Zhao Zuchao, registered in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongzheng. He ranked seventy-fourth in the family order and was thirty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dajin, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Weilian; his father was Jisong, granted the honorary title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother, née Wu, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zushu and Zudu, the latter a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his younger brothers were Zujian, Zupeng (a jinshi of the same examination cohort), Zushu (a Metropolitan Examination graduate, gongshi), and Zuwu (also a gongshi). He married a woman née Jin. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Min, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the prefectural Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Renfu. He ranked second in the family order and was twenty-six years old, born on the nineteenth day of the intercalary tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongshu; his grandfather was Lang; his father was Jingming; and his mother was née Yang. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Gao. He married a woman née Yang. He placed fifty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Yilin, registered in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhongwen. He ranked seventh in the family order and was thirty-four years old, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongren; his grandfather was Deliang; his father was Di; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yifeng, and his younger brother was Yigao. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Chong, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruxi. He ranked first in the family order and was forty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhi; his grandfather was Kan; his father was Congliang, a Chief Clerk; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Kuan, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, and Cai. He married a woman née Gu. He placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Jingxian 郭敬賢, registered in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xiyao, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Mingzhe, his father Song, and his mother née Huang. His father was living; his younger brother was Jingzong. He married a woman née Jin. He placed third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Menglong 梁夢龍, registered in Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Qianji, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Zhao was an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather Ze was a sacrificial official (shengjiguan); and his father Xiang was an annual tribute student. His father's former wife was née Hao, his mother née Cui, and his stepmother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Mengxiong, Mengbi, and Mengling. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed 126th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Yu 齊遇, registered in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military artisan household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shibin, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather Xiang was a Command Registrar; his grandfather Ying was posthumously granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; and his father Zhilong was an Office Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother was née Fang and was living. His elder brothers were Renjie, a Prefect, and Mai and Xun, both National University students; his younger brothers were Di, Shi, Da, Dai, Zun, Bian, and Jin. He married a woman née Xie and subsequently a woman née Fang. He placed 113th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 378th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Cha 鄧察, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household, was a native of Changshu County, and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mingqing, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yin, his grandfather Minghe, his father Ling, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Huang. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Daoguang, registered in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zifu; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his grandfather was Lu; his father was Kan; and his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brothers were Daochong and Daolong. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Tao. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Rujian, registered in the Nanjing Left Guard of the Rear Garrison, belonged to a military household and was a native of Wuxi County in the directly administered territory. He was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tiqian; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the ninth day of the intercalary tenth month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather was Yue; his father was Qing; his father's former wife was née Zhou; and his mother was née Yuan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rucheng, Ruqi, Ruyuan, and Rujie. He married a woman née Sun. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ying Mingde, registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zaiming; he ranked second in birth order and was aged forty, born on the fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather was Wei; his father was Jing; and his mother was née Zhao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jingde, and his younger brothers were Zhongde and Maode. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qiu, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shaoye; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Song; his grandfather was Shiji; his father was Yue; and his mother was née Gong. His parents and grandparents were living. He married a woman née Deng. He placed fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳遵晦〔貫浙江杭州府錢塘縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字明仲，行二，年三十四，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖政，祖宗裕〔封刑部主事〕，父鼎〔布政司左參議〕，母顧氏。慈侍下，兄夢登，弟遵道，娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第八十八名，會試第一百三十六名。

鈔介〔貫河南彰德衛，軍籍，府學生，治書經，字石賓，行一，年三十七，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖全，祖貫，父奇〔知縣〕，母郝氏。具慶下，弟員、胤、貞、分、稷、科、曾，娶袁氏。河南鄉試第二名，會試第二百五十六名。

曾曰鑑〔貫直隸德州衛，軍籍，山東平陽府寧國縣人，國子生，治書經，字萬甫，行一，年三十九，四月十四日生〕。曾祖倬，祖淳，父乾，母王氏。具慶下，弟鑛、鉤、銓，娶宋氏。山東鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百九十一名。

謝鵬舉〔貫湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣，厨籍，縣學生，治易經，字仲南，行四，年三十八，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖思恭，祖明，父寬，嫡母王氏，生母張氏。慈侍下，兄鵬程、鵬升，娶全氏。湖廣鄉試第十七名，會試第一百九十七名。
translation_en:
Wu Zunhui, registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Mingzhong. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Zongyu, was granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Ding, was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother was née Gu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Mengdeng and his younger brother Zundao. He married a woman née Xu. He ranked eighty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chao Jie, registered in Zhangde Guard, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shibin. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather, Guan; his father, Qi, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Hao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuan, Yin, Zhen, Fen, Ji, Ke, and Zeng [the division of these names is uncertain: 員胤貞分稷科曾, ?]. He married a woman née Yuan. He ranked second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Yuejian, registered in Dezhou Guard, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a native of Ningguo County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shandong [the geographical designation is doubtful, ?]. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wanfu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-nine and born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhuo; his grandfather, Chun; his father, Qian; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kuang, Gou, and Quan. He married a woman née Song. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Pengju, registered in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a cook household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongnan. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sigong; his grandfather, Ming; and his father, Kuan. His father's principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Pengcheng and Pengsheng. He married a woman née Quan. He ranked seventeenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

鄧廷猷〔貫湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝嘉，行二，年三十，十二月二十二日生〕。曾祖琳，祖澄，父友信，母湯氏。慈侍下，兄廷策，弟廷佩、廷儒、廷序、廷訓、廷弼，娶呂氏。湖廣鄉試第三十名，會試第九十三名。

張大韶〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字鳴德，行一，年二十八，正月初五日生〕。曾祖銑〔贈南京刑部主事〕，祖璧〔教諭〕，父印〔監生〕，母唐氏。具慶下，弟大武〔監生〕、大英、大成，娶凌氏。應天府鄉試第九名，會試第一百三十六名。
translation_en:
Ruan Wenzhong, registered in an artisan household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Yonghe; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyang, his grandfather Zhongqin, his father Feng, and his mother Lady Chen. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. He married Lady Xie. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Mingshi, registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). His courtesy name was Yingqing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Heng and grandfather Liangbi were county magistrates; his father Yue was a county registrar. His mother was Lady Li, and his stepmother Lady He. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Mingshi (鳴時), Mingqian, and Minglong. He married Lady Zhao. He ranked nineteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Tingyou, registered in a military household in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Rujia; he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Cheng, his father Youxin, and his mother Lady Tang. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brother was Tingce; his younger brothers were Tingpei, Tingru, Tingxu, Tingxun, and Tingbi. He married Lady Lü. He ranked thirtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dashao, registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was a subprefectural government student specializing in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Mingde; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Xian was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Bi was an Instructor, and his father Yin was an Imperial University student. His mother was Lady Tang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dawu, an Imperial University student, Daying, and Dacheng. He married Lady Ling. He ranked ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Yuzhi 趙與治, registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daolong; he ranked third in his family and was thirty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yu held an honorary longevity office; his grandfather Kan was an annual tribute student; his father Zhong was an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qia, Zhan, Yuchun, Dahe (a tribute scholar), Hui, Conglian, Nan, Yujing, and Conglu; his younger brothers were Daliang and Yuxian. His wife was née Hua. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Zhiyan 沈志言, registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zimo; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather Wenli held an honorary longevity office; his father was Mei; his father's former wife was née Zhou; and his mother was née Dai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhide, and his younger brothers were Zhizheng and Zhiwen. His wife was née Yu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yuanbin 鄭源彬, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruyi; he ranked seventh in his family and was twenty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Mengjin was an Instructor; his grandfather was Shuding; his father was Xixiu; his mother was née Lin; and his stepmother was also née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yuanlin, and his wife was née Zeng. He placed forty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shanqing 徐善慶, registered in a civilian household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuanzhen; he ranked sixth in his family and was twenty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yi and grandfather Xiu both held honorary longevity offices; his father was Jun; his mother was née Xu; and his stepmother was née Yuan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Tang, □ [illegible], and Zhan; his younger brother was Tongqing. His wife was née Wang. He placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

王希烈〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，縣學附學生，國子生，治詩經，字子忠，行四十，三十二，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖紹肅，祖崇禎，父廷望，母徐氏。重慶下，兄希昂，弟希周、希程、希張、希佐。娶李氏，繼娶戴氏。江西鄉試第九十三名，會試第二百五十八名。

楊綵〔貫虎賁右衛軍籍，江西吉安府泰和縣人，順天府學生，治詩經，字質甫，行三十二，二十五，二月十一日生〕。曾祖興，祖洪，父瑭，母王氏。慈侍下，兄縉、綱、紀、紳。娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第三十二名，會試第二百三名。

吳邦楨〔貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣匠籍，國子生，治易經，字子寧，行三，年三十七，七月初六日生〕。曾祖璋〔封刑部主事，贈中大夫、太僕寺卿〕，祖洪〔南京刑部尚書，贈太子少保〕，父山〔前刑部尚書〕，前母毛氏〔贈淑人〕，母劉氏〔封太淑人〕。慈侍下，兄邦棟〔監生〕、邦材〔監生〕、邦模〔序班，署光祿寺署丞〕，弟邦本〔陰陽正術〕、邦棨〔監生〕、邦棐〔監生〕、邦榮〔監生〕、邦樞、邦表、邦相、邦裴。娶皇甫氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十九名，會試第二百五十九名。

祝世廉〔貫浙江杭州府海寧縣匠籍，國子生，治禮記，字子隅，行二，年三十四，正月初九日生〕。曾祖沔，祖鰲〔知縣〕，父繼倫〔知縣〕，母賈氏。慈侍下，兄世康，弟世庸、世慶、世庠、世廣、世芹、世應。娶周氏。浙江鄉試第九名，會試第十六名。
translation_en:
Wang Xilie 王希烈, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was an additional student of the county school and a student of the Directorate of Education, specializing in the Book of Odes. He ranked fortieth in his family and was aged thirty-two [?; the age marker is missing in the transcription], born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shaosu; his grandfather, Chongzhen; his father, Tingwang; and his mother, née Xu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Xi’ang; his younger brothers were Xizhou, Xicheng, Xizhang, and Xizuo. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Dai. He placed ninety-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Cai 楊綵, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a military household of the Huben Right Guard and was a native of Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Shuntian prefectural school, specializing in the Book of Odes. He ranked thirty-second in his family and was aged twenty-five [?; the age marker is missing in the transcription], born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Hong; his father, Tang; and his mother, née Wang. His mother alone survived of his parents. His elder brothers were Jin, Gang, Ji, and Shen. He married a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Bangzhen 吳邦楨, courtesy name Zining, was registered in an artisan household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, the Metropolitan Region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education, specializing in the Book of Changes. He ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Zhang, received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master of the Palace and Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His grandfather, Hong, was Minister of Justice at Nanjing and was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. His father, Shan, was formerly Minister of Justice. His father’s former wife, née Mao, was posthumously granted the title Shuren; his mother, née Liu, received the title Tai Shuren. His mother alone survived of his parents. His elder brothers were Bangdong and Bangcai, both students of the Directorate of Education, and Bangmo, an Usher serving as acting Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments. His younger brothers were Bangben, an Astrologer; Bangqi, Bangfei, and Bangrong, all students of the Directorate of Education; and Bangshu, Bangbiao, Bangxiang, and Bangpei. He married a woman née Huangfu. He placed 129th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shilian 祝世廉, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in an artisan household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education, specializing in the Book of Rites. He ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Mian; his grandfather, Ao, was a County Magistrate; his father, Jilun, was also a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Jia. His mother alone survived of his parents. His elder brother was Shikang; his younger brothers were Shiyong, Shiqing, Shixiang, Shiguang, Shiqin, and Shiying. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
南軒〔貫陝西西安府渭南縣，軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字叔後，行一，年三十七，正月十五日生〕。曾祖珪，祖金〔教諭，贈戶部郎中〕，父逢吉〔按察司副使〕，母李氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，弟轅、輇、轍，娶裴氏。陝西鄉試第六十五名，會試第二百四十一名。

姜寶〔貫直隸鎮江府丹陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字廷善，行四十二，年四十，八月初九日生〕。曾祖深，祖昕，父金，母孔氏，繼母金氏。慈侍下，兄寯、寀〔歲貢生〕，弟寅、宋，娶劉氏，繼娶賀氏。應天府鄉試第六十九名，會試第三名。

王學顏〔貫湖廣長沙府湘潭縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字少潜，行一，年三十四，五月初六日生〕。曾祖汝霖，祖琦〔知縣〕，父相〔訓導〕，母張氏。嚴侍下，弟學曾、學孟、學周、學朱，娶楊氏，繼娶史氏。湖廣鄉試第三十七名，會試第二百十九名。

趙祖鵬〔貫浙江金華府東陽縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字宗南，行七十六，年三十五，十月二十日生〕。曾祖大欽，祖為潜，父繼機，母郭氏。慈侍下，兄祖崑、祖𥙿、祖元〔刑部主事〕、祖朝〔同科進士〕，弟祖鶚、祖鵾、祖述〔貢士〕、祖舄〔貢士〕，娶郭氏。浙江鄉試第二十七名，會試第四十八名。
translation_en:
Nan Xuan, courtesy name Shuhou, was registered in Weinan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a military household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was thirty-seven sui, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Jin, was an Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Fengji, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Li, held the honorific title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuan, Quan, and Zhe. He married a woman née Pei. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Bao, courtesy name Tingshan, was registered in Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked forty-second in family order and was forty sui, born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen; his grandfather, Xin; and his father, Jin. His mother was née Kong, and his stepmother was née Jin. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jun and Cai, the latter an annual tribute student; his younger brothers were Yin and Song. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née He. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xueyan, courtesy name Shaoqian, was registered in Xiangtan County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was thirty-four sui, born on the sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rulin; his grandfather, Qi, was a Magistrate; and his father, Xiang, was an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Xuezeng, Xuemeng, Xuezhou, and Xuezhu. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zupeng, courtesy name Zongnan, was registered in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked seventy-sixth in family order and was thirty-five sui, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daqin; his grandfather, Weiqian; and his father, Jiji. His mother was née Guo. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zukun, Zuyu, Zuyuan, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and Zuchao, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort. His younger brothers were Zu’e, Zukun, Zushu, and Zuxi; the latter two were tribute scholars (gongshi). He married a woman née Guo. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

瞿晟〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄州黃梅縣，官籍，縣學生，治詩經，字景明，行八，年三十八，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖子暹，祖顯，父廷桂，母王氏。永感下，兄旦、暘、時，弟星〔貢士〕、昉、昇，娶楊氏，繼娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第八十八名，會試第三百八十一名。
translation_en:
Xu Bing, courtesy name Zhongfu, was from Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang; his grandfather, Kai; his father, Ziqiao; and his mother, née Fang. His mother was living, and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jiong; his younger brothers were Yu, Xun, and Wei. He married a woman née Fang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Jizhi, courtesy name Tidao, was from Tongxiang County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, You, a County Registrar. His legal mother was née Gu, and his birth mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiru, Jijing, Jixue, and Jike 繼科, the last an official awaiting selection for appointment; his younger brother was Jike 繼可. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Cen. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Chaoqing, courtesy name Rubi, was from Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the nineteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Bishi; his grandfather, Qing; his father, Wenye; and his mother, née Yang. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Lei. He placed thirty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qu Sheng, courtesy name Jingming, was from Huangmei County, Qizhou Subprefecture, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and registered in an official household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zixian; his grandfather, Xian; his father, Tinggui; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dan, Yang, and Shi; his younger brothers were Xing, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Fang, and Sheng 昇. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed eighty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Dai, registered in a civilian household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shuming; he ranked 119th in his family’s birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shouyong, his grandfather Yu, his father Ling, and his mother née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Taicheng and Daqi, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Rujia, registered in an official household of the Yingyang Guard in Nanjing, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maozhong; he ranked second in his family’s birth order, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Hui, and his father Jing. His father’s former wives were née Chen and née Li; his legal mother was née Ding, and his birth mother née Xiong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruting, his younger brothers were Ruming and Rusheng, and his wife was née Lu. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Ye, registered in a military household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked twenty-fourth in his family’s birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Hou was Administrator of the household of the Prince of Huai, advanced to the honorary ranks of Grand Master for Court Audiences and Junior Governor for Assisting Governance [?]; his grandfather Lian was a Station Master, and his father Guangguo an Assistant Magistrate. His mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi, Tu, and Kan; his younger brothers were Le, Gai, and Qu; and his wife was née Xu. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Weichun, registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, was a native of Jizhou in Zhending Prefecture, in the metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Deqing; he ranked first in his family’s birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Guang had been honorifically appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather Shi was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and his father Lin a District Magistrate. His mother was née Ying. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Weihe, Weiqin, Weian, Weiyi, and Weikang, and his wife was née Yang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Kan 劉侃, registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhengyan, he ranked fifth in his family, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang, his grandfather Huai, his father Yanfu, and his mother née Tian; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bao and Shen, his younger brother Ren, and his wife née Liao. He placed twenty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Yijing 曾一經, registered in a civilian household in Boluo County, Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhengfu, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Yingzhang (an honorary official for longevity), his father Hong, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Xu; parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yilun, Yigui, Yitong, and Yixiu, and his wife was née Ye. He placed thirtieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Nanyue 喻南嶽, registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jifu, he ranked ninth in his family, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hanxing, his grandfather Rui (an honorary official for longevity), his father Yi, his mother née Liu, and his stepmother née Tian; parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Nan𠠬 [second character’s reading uncertain], and his younger brothers were Nanhuang, Nanqiao, Nanjun, Nanhua, Nanji, Nanlu, Nanlin, Nanzhen, and Nandian; his wife was née Deng. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Weiyi 於惟一, registered in an official household in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Defu, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Kuan, and his father Zan; his father’s former wives were née Xu and née Wang, and his mother was née Nan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Song and Weijing, and his wife was née Shu. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

周賢宣〔貫江西吉安府萬安縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字仲含，行二，年四十三，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖秉清，祖古直，父文珎〔荆府大使〕，母劉氏。永感下，兄賢寀，弟賢窠，娶王氏。江西鄉試第八十一名，會試第三百四十名。

孫鋌〔貫錦衣衛官籍，浙江紹興府餘姚縣人，順天府學增廣生，治易經，字文和，行二十五，年二十六，正月十七日生〕。曾祖新〔贈禮部尚書〕，祖燧〔巡撫江西，右副都御史，贈禮部尚書，謚忠烈〕，父陞〔禮部左侍郎〕，母韓氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母楊氏〔封孺人〕。重慶下，兄鐄〔光祿寺署丞〕、鈇〔監生〕、鉝〔貢士〕、鈺〔官生〕、鏊〔監生〕、鑨〔貢士〕，弟鈞、鑛，娶魏氏。順天府鄉試第一名，會試第一百二十三名。
translation_en:
Zhou Xianxuan, registered in a commoner household in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhonghan; he ranked second in his family and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Bingqing; his grandfather was Guzhi; his father was Wenzhen, Office Manager in the household of the Prince of Jing; and his mother was Lady Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xiancai, and his younger brother was Xianke. He married Lady Wang. He placed eighty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Ying’ao, registered in an official household of Qingping Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Rugao County, Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shanfu; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Han, a Prefectural Vice Prefect advanced to the prestige rank of Grand Master for Impartial Counsel; his grandfather was Zhong, a County Magistrate; his father was Yi, a Prefectural Vice Prefect; and his mother was Lady Si. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Ang, a full Battalion Commander, and his younger brother was Yingzhi. He married Lady Li. He placed first in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Shiyong, registered in a commoner household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Fengyao; he ranked thirty-seventh in his family and was aged forty, born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, an honorary official of longevity; his grandfather was Xuan, a tribute student; his father was Cong, a Ceremonial Officer; and his mother was Lady Hou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Shisheng, and his younger brothers were Shiliang and Shihui. He married Lady Fang. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Ting, registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, was a native of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and an added-quota student at the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenhe; he ranked twenty-fifth in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xin, posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites. His grandfather was Sui, Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites and the name Zhonglie, “Loyal and Resolute.” His father was Sheng, Left Vice Minister of Rites. His mother was Lady Han, posthumously granted the title Lady for Service, and his stepmother was Lady Yang, granted the same title. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Huang, an Office Vice Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Fu, a student of the Directorate of Education; Li, a tribute student; Yu, a student admitted by virtue of official family status; Ao, a student of the Directorate of Education; and Long, a tribute student. His younger brothers were Jun and Kuang. He married Lady Wei. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Dahua, courtesy name Yuande, was registered in a civilian household in Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture. An additional student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Lin; his father, Lu; and his mother, née Pan. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Dali, Dazhi, Dajing, Dale, and Dalun. He married a woman née Gao. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Kuan, courtesy name Dehong, was registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was a native of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Min; his father, Yuan; and his mother, née Dai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shang, and his younger brothers were Long, Yin, Cheng, Shou, and Cai. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gui Jiaxiao, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a civilian household in Chengdu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shan and grandfather Maozhi both served as Administration Vice Commissioners in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father Zhu was a District Magistrate; his mother was née Zhuang, and his stepmother was née Yang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jiayi, Jiamo, Jiayou, Jiazhong, and Jiabin; his younger brother was Jialian. He married a woman née Zhuang. He placed seventeenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Liangshu, courtesy name Zibin, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. An additional student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked twenty-third among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao'an; his grandfather, Tai; his father, Xiangqing; and his mother, née Yao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Liangming, and his younger brothers were Liangqi, Liangyong, Liangkai, Liangzhen, and Liangzhao. He married a woman née Ye. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Wang, registered in a military household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University who specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Daojian, he ranked fifth in his family, and he was thirty-nine, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zaixing; his grandfather, Zhen; his father, Yanhui; and his mother, née Liu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Yuan, a county-school Instructor, Li, Zheng, Dan, Yi, and Li; his younger brother was Yi. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yu, registered in a military household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dayou, he ranked fifth in his family, and he was thirty-six, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zi, an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his grandfather, Qing, a county-school Instructor; his father, Yi; and his mother, née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Kun, Qing, Yi, and Wan; his younger brothers were Zhou and Xian. He married a woman née Tang. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Que, registered in a military household in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an attached student of the subprefectural school who specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ziliang, he ranked third in his family, and he was twenty-six, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Zongru; his father, Dun; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wen, an Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, and Min; his younger brother was Ta. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed sixty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Shen, registered in a civilian household in Mianzhu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and originally from Shanghai County, Zhili, was a subprefectural school student who specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Kongzhi, he ranked first in his family, and he was forty-one, born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue, a Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather, Xianmin, Minister of War; his father, Gao, Right Mentor in the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent; and his mother, née Wang, who had been granted the title Lady (ruren). His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Ji, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Yi, Shu, Hai, Han, Xiang, and Shu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十二年進士登科錄

李元泰〔貫雲南雲南中衛軍籍，浙江餘姚縣人，縣學生，治易經，字道隆，行二，年二十五，五月二十九日生〕。曾祖斌，祖浩，父朝相，母陳氏。具慶下，兄元春，娶錢氏。雲南鄉試第三十三名，會試第二百八十九名。

徐師曾〔貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字伯魯，行六，年三十一，四月初五日生〕。曾祖達，祖縉〔縣主簿〕，父朝〔醫學訓科〕，嫡母王氏，生母凌氏。慈侍下，弟師程，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第一百十一名，會試第二十二名。

金立相〔貫浙江台州府臨海縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字道夫，行一十二，年二十七，十二月初七日生〕。曾祖鎬，祖紘〔封南京刑部主事〕，父賁亨〔提學副使〕，母張氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄立愛〔南京刑部主事〕、立敬〔南京兵部主事〕，弟立常，娶柳氏。浙江鄉試第六十九名，會試第一百十四名。

周時中〔貫廣西桂林右衛官籍，山東濟南府臨邑縣人，國子生，治春秋，字從道，行二，年三十二，正月二十二日生〕。曾祖清，祖鏞〔鄉飲賓〕，父瑾〔知縣〕，母丁氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，兄冕〔生員〕，弟建中，娶朱氏。廣西鄉試第十八名，會試第三百六十六名。
translation_en:
Li Yuantai, registered in a military household of Yunnan Central Guard in Yunnan and a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daolong; he ranked second in the family and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Hao, and his father Chaoxiang; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuanchun, and his wife was née Qian. He placed thirty-third in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shizeng, registered in a civilian household of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bolu; he ranked sixth in the family and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Da; his grandfather Jin was a County Registrar, and his father Chao was a Medical Instructor. His legal mother was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Ling. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brother was Shicheng, and his wife was née Chen. He placed 111th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Lixiang, registered in a civilian household of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked twelfth in the family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather Hong was granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, and his father Benheng was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant. His mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Li’ai, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, and Lijing, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War; his younger brother was Lichang. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shizhong, registered in an officer household of Guilin Right Guard in Guangxi and a native of Linyi County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Congdao; he ranked second in the family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather Yong was an honored guest at the community drinking ceremony, and his father Jin was a County Magistrate. His mother was née Ding, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother Mian was a government school student; his younger brother was Jianzhong. His wife was née Zhu. He placed eighteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 366th in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖信　祖閔〔封奉直大夫吏部考功司員外郎〕父鑾〔奉政大夫吏部驗封司郎中〕嫡母君氏〔贈宜人〕生母栢氏

punctuated:
楊一鶚〔貫直隸廣平府曲周縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子薦，行一，年二十七，十月十九日生〕。曾祖廉〔縣主簿〕，祖澤〔州吏目〕，父世爵〔理問〕，母閻氏，繼母閻氏。重慶下，弟一鵬、一鶴、一鳳，聘黃氏。順天府鄉試第一百三十五名，會試第一百二十四名。

孔惟德〔貫河南汝寧府汝陽縣匠籍，縣學生，治詩經，字恒夫，行一，年二十九，十二月二十八日生〕。曾祖文釗，祖鉞，父舉，前母張氏、楊氏，母閆氏。具慶下，弟惟中，娶張氏，繼娶李氏。河南鄉試第五十六名，會試第九十七名。

程金〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字德良，行七，年三十六，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖福榮，祖顯英〔義官〕，父昇，前母汪氏，母閔氏。具慶下，兄鐵、鐸〔省祭官〕、銳、鍾、鍵、鉦，弟鑑、鏞、鎏、鋆、盤、鏊，娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第三十九名，會試第九十名。

王可大〔貫南京錦衣衛鎮撫司籍，直隸蘇州府吳江縣人，國子生，治易經，字元簡，行二，年三十九，六月二十九日生〕。曾祖信，祖閔〔封奉直大夫、吏部考功司員外郎〕，父鑾〔奉政大夫、吏部驗封司郎中〕，嫡母尹氏〔贈宜人〕，生母柏氏。慈侍下，兄可久，弟可立，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第一百十三名，會試第一百二十一名。
translation_en:
Yang Yi'e, registered in a civilian household in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zijian; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-seven sui, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian, a County Registrar; his grandfather was Ze, a Subprefectural Clerk; and his father was Shijue, a Judicial Official. His mother and stepmother were both née Yan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yipeng, Yihe, and Yifeng. He was betrothed to a woman née Huang. He placed 135th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kong Weide, registered in an artisan household in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Hengfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine sui, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhao, his grandfather Yue, and his father Ju. His father's former wives were née Zhang and née Yang; his mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Weizhong. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed fifty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Jin, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Deliang; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Furong; his grandfather was Xianying, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; and his father was Sheng. His father's former wife was née Wang; his mother was née Min. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tie, Duo (a sacrificial attendant), Rui, Zhong, Jian, and Zheng; his younger brothers were Jian, Yong, Liu, Yun, Pan, and Ao. He married a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Keda was registered with the Office of the Commandant of the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yuanjian, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-nine sui, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin. His grandfather Min received the honorary titles Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel. His father Luan was Grand Master for Governance and Director of the Bureau of Honors in the Ministry of Personnel. His legal mother, née Yin, was posthumously awarded the title Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Bai. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Kejiu and his younger brother Keli. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed 113th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.
