張僎〔貫江西饒州府浮梁縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字誠之，行十，年四十一，十一月十六日生〕。曾祖貴賢〔義官〕，祖文通，父瓘，母吳氏。嚴侍下，弟仕、侃、儼，娶王氏。江西鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百五十一名。

臧繼芳〔貫浙江湖州府長興縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字原實，行一，年三十八，十二月二十三日生〕。曾祖瓛，祖維〔副千戶，贈禮部主事〕，父應璧〔貢士，授光祿寺署丞〕，母吳氏。具慶下，弟繼華、繼藎，娶吳氏。浙江鄉試第十七名，會試第二十七名。

張四維〔貫山西平陽府蒲州軍籍，州學生，治易經，字子維，行一，年二十八，五月十二日生〕。曾祖寧，祖誼，父允齡，母王氏。具慶下，弟四端、四教、四事、四象、四術、四輔，娶王氏。山西鄉試第二名，會試第八十三名。

鍾一元〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字太初，行一，年二十九，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖廣，祖秀〔貢士〕，父靈，母姚氏。具慶下，弟一陽、一貞，娶向氏。浙江鄉試第三十五名，會試第八十四名。
translation_en:
Zhang Zhuan, courtesy name Chengzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked tenth in birth order and was aged forty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Guixian, an honorary official; his grandfather was Wentong; his father was Guan; and his mother was née Wu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shi, Kan, and Yan, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zang Jifang, courtesy name Yuanshi, was registered in a civilian household in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Huan; his grandfather was Wei, a Vice Battalion Commander posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Rites; his father was Yingbi, a tribute student appointed Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jihua and Jijin, and his wife was née Wu. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Siwei, courtesy name Ziwei, was registered in a military household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ning; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Yunling; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Siduan, Sijiao, Sishi, Sixiang, Sishu, and Sifu, and his wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Yiyuan, courtesy name Taichu, was registered in a military household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather was Xiu, a tribute student; his father was Ling; and his mother was née Yao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yiyang and Yizhen, and his wife was née Xiang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

周鑑〔貫陝西平凉府儀衛司軍籍，江西萍鄉縣人，府學生，治詩經，字子明，行四，年二十四，十一月二十一日生〕。曾祖允行，祖亮，父尚仁，前母趙氏，母李氏。具慶下，兄欽、銳、鐸，娶白氏。陝西鄉試第一名，會試第二百二十三名。

曽日傑〔貫江西建昌府南城縣匠籍，府學生，治詩經，字國佐，行十二，年二十八，三月十八日生〕。曾祖榮〔府檢校〕，祖菖，父禧，母饒氏，繼母萬氏。重慶下，弟傅，娶錢氏。江西鄉試第三十九名，會試第三百八十三名。

丘有嵓〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字孔觀，行一，年三十，九月初八日生〕。曾祖崇，祖璽，父壽民，母林氏。慈侍下，弟有峯、有岊、有峩、有峘、有崟，娶李氏。福建鄉試第七十一名，會試第十八名。

程廷策〔貫直隸徽州府休寧縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字汝揚，行十，年三十二，十二月初十日生〕。曾祖永禎，祖天然，父蓋興，母孫氏。具慶下，兄廷試，弟廷訓、廷龍、廷佐，娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第七十八名，會試第二百九十三名。
translation_en:
Zhou Jian, registered in a military household under the Ceremonial Guard Office of Pingliang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was originally from Pingxiang County, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ziming and ranked fourth in his family. He was twenty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunxing; his grandfather, Liang; and his father, Shangren. His father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qin, Rui, and Duo, and his wife was née Bai. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Rijie, registered in an artisan household in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guozuo, and he ranked twelfth in his family. He was twenty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, a prefectural examiner (jianjiao); his grandfather, Chang; and his father, Xi. His mother was née Rao, and his stepmother was née Wan. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His younger brother was Fu, and his wife was née Qian. He placed thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 383rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Youyan, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Kongguan, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chong; his grandfather, Xi; and his father, Shoumin. His mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Youfeng, Youjie, You’e, Youhuan, and Youyin, and his wife was née Li. He placed seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Tingce, registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruyang, and he ranked tenth in his family. He was thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhen; his grandfather, Tianran; and his father, Gaixing. His mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingshi, and his younger brothers were Tingxun, Tinglong, and Tingzuo. His wife was née Wu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

張誼〔貫浙江紹興府蕭山縣匠籍，國子生，治書經，字宣言，行三，年三十二，三月十六日生〕。曾祖珏，祖幹山〔指揮使〕，父廷桂，母高氏。具慶下，兄謐，弟詞、誥、調、語、諧〔監生〕、試、諒，娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第十六名，會試第十七名。

戴一俊〔貫福建泉州府惠安縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字惟宅，行一，年二十三，九月初九日生〕。曾祖廷讓，祖晟，父珦，母何氏。慈侍下，弟一敬，娶張氏。福建鄉試第六十名，會試第二百五十三名。

translation_en:
Fang Wanyou, courtesy name Ruchu, was from a civilian household registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shujin; his grandfather, Lin, was a county-school Instructor; his father was Zaiyuan, and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wanzai, Wanxiang (annotated “Huolin” [?]), and Wansong, and his younger brother was Jizeng; his wife was née Wu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yi, courtesy name Xuanyan, was from an artisan household registered in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue; his grandfather, Ganshan, was a Commander; his father was Tinggui, and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mi; his younger brothers were Ci, Gao, Tiao, Yu, Xie (a student of the Directorate of Education), Shi, and Liang; his wife was née Huang. He placed sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Yijun, courtesy name Weizhai, was from a military household registered in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-three, and was born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingrang, his grandfather was Sheng, his father was Xiang, and his mother was née He. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Yijing; his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Shu [?], courtesy name Zhonghe, was from a civilian household registered in Ren County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a prefectural-school student specializing in the Book of Documents; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Qi, was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his grandfather was Zong, his father was Wei, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zhen and Shu (a sacrificial official, shengjiguan [?]); his wife was née Liu. He placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

凌立〔貫浙江杭州府錢塘縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字子中，行一，年三十四，九月二十七日生〕。曾祖高〔衞知事〕，祖恩，父桂，母張氏〔旌表節婦〕。慈侍下。娶朱氏。浙江鄉試第三十一名，會試第二百五十名。
translation_en:
Lin Jing, registered in a civilian household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Quecheng; he ranked third in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongshuo, posthumously or honorifically appointed Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Biao, a prefect; his father was Bi, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu and Min; his younger brothers were Xiao, a student of the Directorate of Education, Mu, and Chi. He married a woman née Wu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Tun, registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zihou; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather was Guan, and his father was Shi, a tribute student; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yue and Yao; his younger brothers were Rong, Hui, Xuan, Lan, Huang, Tun [?—the transcription repeats his own given name], Jiao, and Lian. He married a woman née Tang. He placed fifth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dechong, registered in a civilian household in Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Benxu; he ranked twelfth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianqi, his grandfather was Guan, and his father was Yu; his mother was née Zou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Lang, and his younger brother was Deming. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ling Li, registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gao, an administrative clerk in a guard; his grandfather was En, and his father was Gui. His mother, née Zhang, had received official recognition as a chaste widow. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Wenxing, courtesy name Weicheng, was registered in a military household of Dingbian Guard in the Metropolitan Region and was a native of Puzhou, Shanxi. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third in family order and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Derang, his grandfather Qi, his father Qing, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ru and Wenming, and his wife was née Li. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yongguang, courtesy name Chengfu, was registered in a civilian household of Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked twenty-third in family order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Jiang, his father Pao, a tribute student, and his mother née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yonggui; his younger brothers were Yongjian, Yongqian, Yongxiu, Yongxiang, Yongxian, Yongqi, and Yongdeng. His wife was née Tang. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chunshi, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a civilian household of Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A county school student specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked first in family order and was thirty-six years old, born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Meixing, his grandfather Fucheng, his father Lan, and his mother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chunshu and Chunxuan, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhengwei, courtesy name Yili, was registered in a civilian household of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first in family order and was thirty-four years old, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yuqi, his grandfather Daxun, his father Yuanzong, and his mother née Tu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zhengbang and Zhengqing, his younger brother Zhengxin, and his wife née Luo. He placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 317th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Yong, registered in Xingzi County, Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruyuan; he ranked twenty-first among his male relatives in his generation, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunyu; his grandfather, Huan, was a Guard Registrar; his father was He, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mi, and his younger brothers were Yi, Lian, and Qian. His wife was née Wang. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Shiyan, registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shimei; he ranked seventeenth among his male relatives in his generation, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dinghe; his grandfather, Fu, was posthumously awarded the title of Secretary in the Ministry of War; his father, Yue, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Zhuang, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Li and Yin, both students of the Imperial University, and Qi; his younger brother was Yong. His wife was née Zhu. He placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third class: 295 men, granted the status of graduates assimilated to metropolitan graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Li Donghua, registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingxiao; he ranked ninth among his male siblings and cousins and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Huan, a Director of County Schools; his grandfather was Fu; his father was En; and his mother was née Tu. Both parents were living. His younger brother Dongping was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Wenfu, registered in an artisan household of the Left Jinwu Guard and a native of Yangqu County, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongchen; he ranked first among his male siblings and cousins and was aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather was Zhi, honorifically appointed a Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites; his father was Jun, a Vice Commissioner of a Salt Distribution Commission; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wendu, Wenbi, Wenshou, Wenhe, and Wenkai. He married a woman née Fan. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Jizeng, registered in an official household in Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shouyue; he ranked third among his male siblings and cousins and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Kui, a student of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather was Ye, a holder of honorary official status for longevity; his father was Guangsu, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jimeng and Jiyan; his younger brothers were Jiyin, Jiyi, Jiqi, and Jiji. He married a woman née Han. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gu Zhangzhi, courtesy name Zixing, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Kunshan County. An attached student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather Jian held the honorary title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; his father Ji was Supervising Secretary in that office; and his mother, née Lu, held the title of Lady (ruren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Zong was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhongji, courtesy name Jiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Sheng, his father Hua, and his mother née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bomei. He married a woman née Tang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Ruyu, courtesy name Mengchun, was registered in a civilian household in Yun County, Yunyang Prefecture, Huguang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Cong held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Huai, his father Xin, and his mother née Zuo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Ruchun, Ruquan, and Rubi. He married a woman née Zhong and subsequently became betrothed to another woman née Zhong. He placed ninetieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Min, courtesy name Ruxiu, was registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yangao, his grandfather Binglin, and his father Wenzao; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qi, Xiao, and She. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Jing, registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a military household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziyi. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Fu; his father's former wife and his mother were both née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shu, Ce, and Mian. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventy-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 390th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Cheng, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zongluo. Third in birth order, he was aged fifty and was born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, Academician of the Hanlin Academy, posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of Rites and the posthumous name Wenyi; his grandfather was Mao (𢘅), Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing. His father was Jiao and his mother née Mao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Ke, a tribute student (gongshi), and Zhi; his younger brothers were Ji, Mu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort, and Jie. He married a woman née He. He placed eighty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Gun, registered in Neixiang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zitian. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-three and was born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, a prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather was Hou, a District Magistrate; his father was Zongmu, a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yin, Rui, and Yu. He married a woman née Hu. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 352nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shilai, registered in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weixiu. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shushen, a Registrar, posthumously granted the title of Gentleman of the Forest of Letters; his grandfather was Rongzan, his father Bingtai, and his mother née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shijiao and Shiyong. He married a woman née Yin. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Kuang 徐爌 was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Mingyu, ranked third among his brothers, and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tingrui, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Shouyuan; his father was Gai; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhao and Jiong, and his younger brothers were Lie, Lian, Can, and Tao. His wife was née Wu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shuhe 李叔和 was registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Jiefu, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jixuan; his grandfather was Jun; his father was Gong; his legal mother was née Zhang; and his birth mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Boxing, and his younger brothers were Zhongfa and Zhongda. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Yingqi 蔣應期 was registered in a military household in Quanzhou Subprefecture, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ruchang, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-three years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ziren; his grandfather was Yonggang; his father was Shike, an unranked county official; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingqian, Yingpin, and Yingdeng. His wife was née Hu. He placed forty-sixth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Yuezhuo 曹曰灼 was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he had the courtesy name Yonghui, ranked first among his brothers, and was forty-two years old, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Liangying; his grandfather was Heng 𢘆, an Assistant Instructor posthumously granted the title of Vice Commander of a Wardens' Office; and his father was Quan 犬 [?], Vice Commander of a Wardens' Office. His mother was née Mao, posthumously granted the title Lady (Ruren), and his stepmother was née Qu. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother was Kui, a Prefect; his younger brothers were Xuan, Wei, Huan, Rong, Yu, Zhao, Jiong, Lian, and Yi. His wife was née Qu 瞿. He placed thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Sanxi, courtesy name Huaiguo, was from Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, an assistant prefect; his grandfather was Xuan; his father was Shou; and his mother was née Pan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sanjie, Sanpin, and Sangu, and his wife was née Zong. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan You, courtesy name Gongfu, was from Baodi County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather was Li; his father was Zhang; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yin and Gu, and his wife was née Peng. He placed sixty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Yuanji, courtesy name Jingzhi, was from Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and belonged to a civilian household. A supplementary student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongzan; his grandfather was Shuhua; his father was Jiwei; his mother was née Zhou; and his stepmother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuanjian and Yuanzhong, his younger brother was Yuanshan, and his wife was née Xu. He placed thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qiqin, courtesy name Shimin, was from Songzi County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and belonged to a civilian household. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benyi, a county magistrate; his grandfather was Xiangzhi, a subprefect; his father was Tianzhang; and his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Qixian, and his wife was née Hu. He placed sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Qiuke 張求可 was registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zhongfu, ranked second in his family, and was aged thirty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizong, posthumously appointed a case reviewer; his grandfather was Gong, a bureau director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his father was Yu, and his mother was née Song. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Shike and Jike; his younger brothers were Jianke, Qike, Xingke, Jinke, Qike 期可, Yongke, and Fuke. His wife was née Ji. He placed fifty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chunfang 李春芳 was registered in Qinshui County, in a prefecture whose name is illegible [?], in a civilian household. He was an Imperial University student; the following five characters are illegible, followed by 實 (shi) [?]. He ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather’s name is illegible; his father was Jie, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents survived. His younger brothers were Liangshi, Liangxiang, Jifang, Shifang, and Liangchen. His wife was née Niu. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Kui 陳奎 was registered in Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. An added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Ruxing, ranked eighth in his family, and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren, his grandfather was Han, his father was Zhe, and his mother was née Liu. His mother alone survived. His younger brother was Bi. His wife was née Guo; his subsequent wife was née Qi. He placed fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuemo 王學謨 was registered in Chaoyi County, Tongzhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in an artisan household. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ziyang, ranked fourth in his family, and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenmei, his grandfather was Kun, his father was Shiqing, and his mother was née Liang. Both parents survived. His elder brothers were Xueshi 學詩, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Xuecheng; Xuegu, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Xuegao; Xueshi 學仕; and Xuesong. His younger brothers were Xuerang, Huaxing, and Xuehui. His wife was née Yang. He placed fortieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

鍾沂〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字宗魯，行一，年四十，十月二十九日生〕。曾祖叔順，祖玉潤，父彩，母何氏，繼母熊氏。具慶下，弟沐、洽、浹、治、淳、滼，娶熊氏。江西鄉試第二十五名，會試第三百九名。

張九功〔貫山西沁州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字惟敘，行二，年二十六，七月十八日生〕。曾祖顥〔監生〕，祖好古〔監生，贈文林郎、監察御史〕，父鵬〔大理寺右寺丞〕，母周氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄九思，弟九式〔監生〕、九儀、九德，娶劉氏。山西鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百二十七名。

唐自化〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣竈籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯咸，行二，年四十三，八月二十日生〕。曾祖墉〔贈兵部車駕司主事〕，祖祚〔壽官〕，父𢢀，母劉氏，繼母戴氏、錢氏。永感下，兄自明〔監生〕，弟自得〔監生〕、自皇、自治〔監生〕、自阜、自脩、自然，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第十九名，會試第一百九十六名。
translation_en:
Wu Chengtao, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in an artisan household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Hong was Grand Master for Assisting Goodness and Minister of Justice at Nanjing, posthumously awarded the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his grandfather Shan was a former Minister of Justice; his father Bangdong was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Xu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother Chengxi was a student admitted by virtue of an official’s privilege; his younger brothers were Chengguang, Chengzhao, Chengqian, Chengmo, Chenglian, Chengfu, and Chenglie. He married a woman née Jin. He ranked 123rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Yi, courtesy name Zonglu, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shushun, his grandfather Yurun, and his father Cai; his mother was née He and his stepmother née Xiong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mu, Qia, Jia, Zhi, Chun, and Fan; he married a woman née Xiong. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiugong, courtesy name Weixu, was registered in a civilian household in Qin Subprefecture, Shanxi. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Hao was an Imperial University student; his grandfather Haogu was an Imperial University student, posthumously awarded the titles Gentleman for Cultivated Service and Investigating Censor; his father Peng was Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; and his mother, née Zhou, was granted the title Lady. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Jiusi; his younger brothers were Jiushi, an Imperial University student, Jiuyi, and Jiude. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Zihua, courtesy name Boxian, was registered in a salt-producing household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Yong was posthumously awarded the office of Secretary in the Bureau of Equipment of the Ministry of War; his grandfather Zuo held an honorary official title granted for longevity; his father’s name is transcribed as 𢢀 [?]; his mother was née Liu, and his successive stepmothers were née Dai and née Qian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Ziming was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Zide, an Imperial University student, Zihuang, Zizhi, an Imperial University student, Zifu, Zixiu, and Ziran. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十二年進士登科錄
text:
江北
貫順天府覇州民籍江西廣信府鉛山縣人國子生
治書經字拱北行四年二十七十月二十一日生
曾祖均善祖源父謙〔訓導〕前母苗氏李氏母王氏
慈侍下兄西東〔知縣〕南〔訓導〕娶王氏繼娶金氏
順天府鄉試第五十九名會試第一百六十名
吳可行
貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍宜興縣人國子生
治易經字子言行十一二十七十一月十四日生
曾祖昊祖禮〔封南京戶部主事〕父性〔南京禮部主事〕前母杜氏〔贈安人〕母段氏〔封安人〕
具慶下兄讓闇註譔諍譽弟時行見行中行尚行同行娶陳氏
應天府鄉試第二十二名會試第六名
===
陸泰
貫浙江寧波府鄞縣軍籍國子生
治易經字惟安行一年三十二八月初十日生
曾祖培祖偲父鈳母包氏
重慶下弟水榮槩娶水氏
浙江鄉試第六十三名會試第三百二十八名
馬自強
貫陝西西安府同州軍籍國子生
治春秋字體乾行二年四十一十一月初二日生
曾祖文祖通〔知縣贈文林郎〕父珍〔縣丞〕母李氏〔封孺人〕繼母張氏
具慶下兄秉中〔驛丞〕駙〔監生〕馬堂馬芥〔訓導〕馬慮馬□弟自脩自進自道自省娶李氏
陝西鄉試第一名會試第二百九十二名
alt_text:
江北
貫順天府□州民籍江西廣信府鉛山縣人　國子生
治書經字拱北行四年二十七十月二十一日生
曾祖均善　祖源　父謙〔訓導〕　前母田氏　李氏　母王氏
慈侍下　兄西　東〔知縣〕　南　〔導〕　娶王氏　繼娶金氏
順天府鄉試第五十九名　會試第一百六十名
吳可行
貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍宜興縣人　國子生
治易經字子言行一年二十七十一月十四日生
曾祖昊　祖禮〔封南京戶部主事〕　父性〔南京戶部郎中〕　前母杜氏〔贈安人〕　母談氏〔封安人〕
具慶下　兄讓　聞　註　譔　論　詩　詧　弟時行　衍　行忠　行尚　行同　行　娶陳氏
應天府鄉試第二十三名　會試第六名
===
陸泰
貫浙江寧波府鄞縣竈籍　國子生
治易經字惟安行一年三十二八月初十日生
曾祖培　祖偲　父鋼　母包氏
重慶下　弟水　榮　聚　娶水氏
浙江鄉試第六十三名　會試第三百二十八名
馬自強
貫陝西西安府同州軍籍　國子生
治春秋字體乾行一年四十一十一月初二日生
曾祖文　祖通〔知縣贈文林郎〕　父麻〔縣丞〕　母李氏〔封孺人〕　繼母張氏
具慶下　兄秉中〔驛丞〕　□□〔附監生〕　□□〔驛丞〕　弟自脩　自進　自道　自省　娶李氏
陝西鄉試第一名　會試第二百九十二名
punctuated:
江北，貫順天府覇州民籍，江西廣信府鉛山縣人，國子生，治書經，字拱北，行四，年二十七，十月二十一日生。曾祖均善，祖源，父謙〔訓導〕，前母苗氏、李氏，母王氏。慈侍下，兄西、東〔知縣〕、南〔訓導〕，娶王氏，繼娶金氏。順天府鄉試第五十九名，會試第一百六十名。

吳可行，貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍，宜興縣人，國子生，治易經，字子言，行十一，二十七，十一月十四日生。曾祖昊，祖禮〔封南京戶部主事〕，父性〔南京禮部主事〕，前母杜氏〔贈安人〕，母段氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄讓、闇、註、譔、諍、譽，弟時行、見行、中行、尚行、同行，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第二十二名，會試第六名。

陸泰，貫浙江寧波府鄞縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字惟安，行一，年三十二，八月初十日生。曾祖培，祖偲，父鈳，母包氏。重慶下，弟水、榮、槩，娶水氏。浙江鄉試第六十三名，會試第三百二十八名。

馬自強，貫陝西西安府同州軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字體乾，行二，年四十一，十一月初二日生。曾祖文，祖通〔知縣贈文林郎〕，父珍〔縣丞〕，母李氏〔封孺人〕，繼母張氏。具慶下，兄秉中〔驛丞〕、駙〔監生〕、馬堂、馬芥〔訓導〕、馬慮、馬□，弟自脩、自進、自道、自省，娶李氏。陝西鄉試第一名，會試第二百九十二名。
translation_en:
Jiang Bei was registered in a civilian household in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Gongbei and ranked fourth in birth order. He was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junshan; his grandfather, Yuan; and his father, Qian, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wives were née Miao and née Li; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xi, Dong (a District Magistrate), and Nan (an Assistant Instructor). He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Jin. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Kexing was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Yixing County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ziyan and ranked eleventh in birth order. He was twenty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Li, who received the honorary title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Xing, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites. His father's former wife, née Du, was posthumously awarded the title Lady of Tranquility; his mother, née Duan, was awarded the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rang, An, Zhu, Zhuan, Zheng, and Yu; his younger brothers were Shixing, Jianxing, Zhongxing, Shangxing, and Tongxing. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Tai was registered in a military household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Wei'an and ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pei; his grandfather, Cai; his father, Ke; and his mother, née Bao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shui, Rong, and Gai. He married a woman née Shui. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 328th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Ziqiang was registered in a military household in Tongzhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Tiqian and ranked second in birth order. He was forty-one, born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather, Tong, a District Magistrate posthumously awarded the title Gentleman of the Forest of Literature; and his father, Zhen, a District Vice Magistrate. His mother, née Li, was awarded the title Lady; his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bingzhong (a Postal Station Master), Fu (an Imperial University student), Ma Tang [?], Ma Jie [?] (an Assistant Instructor), Ma Lü [?], and Ma □ [?]; his younger brothers were Zixiu, Zijin, Zidao, and Zixing. He married a woman née Li. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十二年進士登科錄
text:
蔡本端〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍府學附學生治易經字幼貞行五年三十五五月二十日生〕
曾祖榮祖文鑛父浩〔知州〕嫡母陳氏生母林氏
永感下弟本瑞本顓娶林氏
福建鄉試第二十五名會試第一百八十七名
葉可成〔貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣民籍縣學生治書經字懋學行九年三十一八月二十八日生〕
曾祖芳〔廣西布政司副理問贈中憲大夫太僕寺少卿〕祖紳〔尚寶司少卿〕父旦母汝氏
具慶下兄可久可大敘古可觀〔陰陽正術〕可守允弟可與可仕可畏娶盧氏
應天府鄉試第九十二名會試第二百八十名
===
梁淮〔貫錦衣衛鎮撫司軍籍浙江金華縣人順天府學增廣生治詩經字中行行三年三十十月二十六日生〕
曾祖宗德祖景輝父宣母陳氏
嚴侍下兄清弟澄娶俞氏
順天府鄉試第三十名會試第三百三十名
李瑶〔貫山西平陽府解州民籍州學生治禮記字溫甫行二年二十一正月二十二日生〕
曾祖威祖素父成郊母孫氏
具慶下兄瑞弟珍琬娶丘氏
山西鄉試第五名會試第三百八十名
alt_text:
蔡本端貫福建福州府閩縣民籍 府學附學生
治易經字幼貞行五年三十五五月二十日生
曾祖榮 祖文鑛 父浩〔知州〕 生母林氏
嫡母陳氏
永感下 弟本瑞 本顯 娶林氏
福建鄉試第二十五名 會試第一百八十七名
葉可成貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣民籍 縣學生
治書經字懋學行九年三十一八月二十八日生
曾祖芳〔廣西布政司副理問贈資善大夫刑部尚書〕 祖紳〔尚寶司少卿〕 父旦 母汝氏
具慶下 兄可久 可大 敘〔貢士〕 觀〔陰陽正術〕 弟可學 可允 可與 可仕 可畏 娶盧氏
應天府鄉試第九十二名 會試第一百八十名
===
梁淮貫錦衣衛鎮撫司軍籍浙江金華縣人 順天府學增廣生
治詩經字中行行三年三十十月二十六日生
曾祖宗德 祖景輝 父宣 母陳氏
嚴侍下 兄清 弟澄 娶俞氏
順天府鄉試第三十名 會試第三百三十名
李瑶貫山西平陽府解州民籍 州學生
治禮記字溫甫行一年二十一正月二十二日生
曾祖威 祖素 父成〔郎〕 母孫氏
具慶下 兄瑞 弟珍 琥 娶丘氏
山西鄉試第五名 會試第三百八十名
punctuated:
蔡本端〔貫福建福州府閩縣，民籍，府學附學生，治易經，字幼貞，行五，年三十五，五月二十日生〕。曾祖榮，祖文鑛，父浩〔知州〕，嫡母陳氏，生母林氏。永感下，弟本瑞、本顓，娶林氏。福建鄉試第二十五名，會試第一百八十七名。

葉可成〔貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字懋學，行九，年三十一，八月二十八日生〕。曾祖芳〔廣西布政司副理問，贈中憲大夫、太僕寺少卿〕，祖紳〔尚寶司少卿〕，父旦，母汝氏。具慶下，兄可久、可大、敘古、可觀〔陰陽正術〕、可守、允，弟可與、可仕、可畏，娶盧氏。應天府鄉試第九十二名，會試第二百八十名。

梁淮〔貫錦衣衛鎮撫司，軍籍，浙江金華縣人，順天府學增廣生，治詩經，字中行，行三，年三十，十月二十六日生〕。曾祖宗德，祖景輝，父宣，母陳氏。嚴侍下，兄清，弟澄，娶俞氏。順天府鄉試第三十名，會試第三百三十名。

李瑶〔貫山西平陽府解州，民籍，州學生，治禮記，字溫甫，行二，年二十一，正月二十二日生〕。曾祖威，祖素，父成郊，母孫氏。具慶下，兄瑞，弟珍、琬，娶丘氏。山西鄉試第五名，會試第三百八十名。
translation_en:
Cai Benduan 蔡本端 was registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household and was an attached student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Youzhen, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the twentieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Wenkuang; and his father, Hao, a department magistrate. His legal mother was Lady Chen, and his birth mother was Lady Lin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Benrui and Benzhuan. He married Lady Lin. He placed twenty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Kecheng 葉可成 was registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Maoxue, and he ranked ninth among his brothers. He was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Fang, was Vice Judicial Commissioner in the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission, posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Palace Counsel and the office of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His grandfather, Shen, was Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Seals; his father was Dan, and his mother was Lady Ru. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kejiu, Keda, Xugu, Keguan, Chief Astrologer, Keshou, and Yun; his younger brothers were Keyu, Keshi, and Kewei. He married Lady Lu. He placed ninety-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Huai 梁淮 was registered in a military household under the Office of the Discipline Officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Jinhua County, Zhejiang. He was an added-quota student at the Shuntian prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongxing, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongde; his grandfather, Jinghui; his father, Xuan; and his mother, Lady Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Qing, and his younger brother was Cheng. He married Lady Yu. He placed thirtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 330th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yao 李瑶 was registered in Jie Department, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household and was a student at the departmental school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Wenfu, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was twenty-one years old, born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei; his grandfather, Su; his father, Chengjiao; and his mother, Lady Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rui, and his younger brothers were Zhen and Wan. He married Lady Qiu. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 380th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十二年進士登科錄
text:
趙桐〔貫山西平陽府絳州匠籍州學生治書經字汝陽行一年二十七三月二十四日生〕
曾祖演祖統父玭母馮氏
具慶下娶毛氏繼娶靳氏
山西鄉試第二名會試第二百二十五名
秦禾〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣民籍國子生治書經字子實行三年三十二四月二十三日生〕
曾祖永孚〔旌表孝子〕祖鏜〔南京都察院都事〕父淮〔歲貢生〕母周氏
嚴侍下兄采〔縣丞〕梁〔吏科給事中〕弟𧀲楶澯棐楠木林森娶葛氏
應天府鄉試第四十四名會試第一百八十九名

translation_en:
Zhao Tong, courtesy name Ruyang, was registered in an artisan household in Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the department school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Tong, his father Pin, and his mother née Feng. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Mao and subsequently a woman née Jin. He ranked second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin He, courtesy name Zishi, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Yongfu was officially honored for filial piety; his grandfather Tang was Office Manager in the Nanjing Censorate; his father Huai was an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Cai, a County Vice Magistrate, and Liang, a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel. His younger brothers were 𧀲 [name reading uncertain], Jie, Can, Fei, Nan, Mu, Lin, and Sen. He married a woman née Ge. He ranked forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Ren, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in an officer household of Longxiang Guard and was a native of Huairou County, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Jie, grandfather Lao, and father Lu were each Vice Battalion Commanders granted the title General of Military Strategy. His mother, née Cui, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Li was Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Ru, courtesy name Zichun, was registered in an artisan household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Fu held honorary official status for public benefaction; his grandfather was Zeng, his father Feng, and his mother née Feng. His parents and grandparent generation were living. His elder brother was Jie, and his younger brothers were Ren, Wei, and Dai. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 335th in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃休泰〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，府學附學生，治書經，字啓大，行八，年三十一，十二月二十三日生〕。曾祖洙〔訓導〕，祖希寬，父景禮，前母徐氏，母張氏。永感下，兄休賁、休復、有濟、休咸、休徵，弟休兆、休光，娶吳氏。福建鄉試第三名，會試第二百四十八名。

translation_en:
Wang Ruda, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhixing, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Chun, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Shitai, and his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living; his wife was née Zhou. He placed eighty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Lian, registered in Zunhua County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Congshang, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was En; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Wenyu; his mother was née Guo, and his stepmother was née Peng. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Zhang and Hu, his younger brother was Ban, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fiftieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xiutai, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Qida, he ranked eighth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhu, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Xikuan; his father was Jingli; his father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Xiuben, Xiufu, Youji, Xiuxian, and Xiuzheng, his younger brothers were Xiuzhao and Xiuguang, and his wife was née Wu. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Congyi, registered in Changyuan County, Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zongxian, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai; his grandfather was Xun, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Ti, a Messenger; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living; his younger brother was Congzhong, and his wife was née Yin. He placed 127th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 394th in the Metropolitan Examination.

司馬初〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣儒籍，縣學生，治詩經，字元甫，行一，年四十一，九月初二日生〕。曾祖壇，祖公黻〔贈刑部主事〕，父相〔按察司僉事〕，母趙氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，弟祿、法、止、收、吉、禮，娶章氏。浙江鄉試第六十一名，會試第三十八名。

translation_en:
Zheng Mao 鄭茂 was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a supplementary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shiyuan. He ranked fourteenth among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-eight sui old, born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jie, a county-school instructor; his grandfather was Ke; and his father was Jingdao, a county magistrate. His father's principal wife and his birth mother were both née Lin. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Shu, Wei, Chun, Zao (a postal-station master), Fang, Jing, Yun (an investigating censor), Chai, Lu (a provincial sacrificial official [省祭官; ?]), Shen, Yao, Xiao, and Jian; his younger brother was Ai. His wife was née Lin. He placed thirty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Wenguang 楊文光 was registered in a civilian household in Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was an added-quota student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Chengfu. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-six sui old, born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Mian, a prefectural judge; his grandfather was Shunqing, a commander in a Military Police Office; and his father was Lan, a subprefectural magistrate. His mother was née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Wensheng, Wenzheng, and Wenxun. His wife was née Yu. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sima Chu 司馬初 was registered in a scholar household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanfu. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was forty-one sui old, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tan; his grandfather was Gongfu, posthumously granted the title of secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his father was Xiang, an assistant surveillance commissioner. His mother, née Zhao, had been granted the title of Lady of Peace. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Lu, Fa, Zhi, Shou, Ji, and Li. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xunyan 張巽言 was registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyi. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-six sui old, born on the eleventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Peng, a county magistrate; and his father was Jiahe. His mother was née Huang, and his stepmother was née Ma. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 354th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Dong, registered in Shangqiu County, Guide Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ziyuan, he was second in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Jue, was an Investigating Censor; his father was Zhi and his mother née Lu, both deceased; his elder brother was Nan, his younger brother was Xi, and his wife was née Zhu; he ranked thirty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Maoguan, registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Kongzhi, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Jinglong, was an Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Lianggui, was a School Instructor; his father was Shan and his mother née Pan, with his mother surviving and his father deceased; his younger brothers were Maoming, Maozhang, and Maoxian, and his wife was née Lin; he ranked fifty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yingwen, registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zihui, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jingshan, his grandfather was An, his father was Mao, and his mother was née Du; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Yingjian and Yingxuan, and his wife was née Zheng; he ranked ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 385th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yukui, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Hongyu, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather was Tingwei, his father was Yuanhou, and his mother was née Li; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Yumen, Yubiao, Yubao, and Yuxiang, and his wife was née Ou; he ranked twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zeng Yuemei, courtesy name Yitiao, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An attached student at the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianfu, his grandfather Lixuan, and his father Tanghui; his mother was née Xiao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Mu, and his wife was née Li. He ranked twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Chaoyi, courtesy name Zhizhi, was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in an artisan household. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Shitai, and his father Hongke; his mother was née Wu. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Chaobin 〔Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice〕; his younger brothers were Chaofu 〔a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort〕, Chaocai 〔tribute scholar (gongshi)〕, Chaos hi [?], Chaohuan, and Chaoshou. His wife was née Xue. He ranked twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yingyuan, courtesy name Wenzheng, was registered in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. An added-quota student at the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng, his grandfather Ming, and his father You; his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Yingkui 〔District Magistrate〕. His first wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Wu. He ranked sixty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 332nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shifeng, courtesy name Yingshao, was registered in Linqing Guard, Shandong, in a military household, and was a native of Jiangzhou, Shanxi. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Qi; his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Shiluan, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xian, courtesy name Jinfu, was registered in a military household of Yingtian Guard, Nanjing, and was a native of Jiangpu County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Luan, his father Qi, and his mother née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chen and his younger brother Qing; his wife was née Yue [?]. He placed sixty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Cha, courtesy name Mingfu, was registered in a civilian household of Wenjiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong was granted the title of Secretary and posthumously granted that of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather Hanzong was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and his father Shi’ang was a Commander of a Police Office. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Cheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yin, Shi, Xuan (Assistant Instructor), Yangqi, Bao (Assistant Instructor), Su (Vice Magistrate of Wan County), Cai, Ning, and Hong (a tribute scholar); his younger brothers were Xian, Chong, Shou, and Chen. His wife was née Wen. He placed thirty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shidi, courtesy name Boxiong, was registered in a civilian household of Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yingchun was Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his grandfather Qi was a Prefectural Registrar, and his father was Yanzong. His legal mother was née Zheng and his birth mother née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Ran. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Kun, courtesy name Huaqing, was registered in a military household of Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Haiyan County. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked seventh among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Zai (Instructor). His father's former wives were née Wu and née Zhou; his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Long (Assistant Instructor), Feng (a student of the Directorate of Education), Ao, Bin, Yin, and Lu; his younger brothers were Lu, Li, He, and Wei. His wife was née Zhong. He placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Qida, courtesy name Ziwei, was registered in a military household in Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. An added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather was Rong, a clerk; his father was Shangcheng; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xu, Cai, and Ji (an annual tribute student), and his younger brother was Luan. His wife was née Ji. He placed forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zhi, courtesy name Wenzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Anlu County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. An attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benyuan; his grandfather was He, an assistant prefect; and his father was Dongxi, a registrar. His legal mother was née Liang, and his birth mother was née Wei. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Qin, and his wife was née Zuo. He placed forty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Yuan, courtesy name Boshi, was registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongming; his grandfather was Jiong; his father was Cailiang, a postal station master; and his mother was née Gong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Han and Wei, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Cunyi, courtesy name Zhiqing, was registered in a military household of Xiangyang Guard, Huguang. He was an instructor at the Confucian school of Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bi; his grandfather was Zhong, a county vice magistrate; his father was Dajing; and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cunren, and his wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qi Yuanfu, of an artisan household registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Xizhou, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pian, his grandfather Ze, his father Shan, and his mother née Zhang; his mother alone was living, his younger brother Yuanzuo was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his wife was née Shao; he placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Meng, of a commoner household registered in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zizheng, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Jing held an honorary official title granted for longevity, his father was Xiang, and his mother was née Tang; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Jie, his younger brother Yi, and his wife née Pan; he placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Rufang, of a military household registered in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weide, he ranked sixth in family birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sizhong, his grandfather Tinghuan, his father Jin, and his mother née Ning; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Rushun and Rufu, and his wife was née Wu; he placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Gan, of a commoner household registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Maoqing, he ranked seventy-first in family birth order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Xuan, his father Ji (commissioner of the Wulang saltworks [?]), and his mother née Wang; his father alone was living, his elder brothers were Lu, Huang, Yu, Zhao, and Jian, and his wife was née Ruan; he placed fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cui Zongyao, registered in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruqin, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was forty-two years old, born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Youneng; and his father, Chaozuo, a Director of Studies. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother née Yuan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zongkong. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently women née Li and Han. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Renhui, registered in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingfu, and he ranked fourth among his brothers. He was forty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dian, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather, Ru; and his father, Yide. His mother was née Lin, and his stepmother née Xue. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Renjie and Renzhong; his younger brothers were Renwei, Renju, Renxian, Yingkui, and Yingyuan. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lang, registered in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongyun, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ting; his grandfather, Rui; and his father, Chengxue, a Prefect. His mother was née Hao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bi; his younger brothers were Xu, Du, and Geng. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Sijiu, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zizheng, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-six years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ru; his grandfather, Wenjie, a Station Master; and his father, Chi, a Registrar. His father’s former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Sida. He married a woman née Zhou (州). He placed twenty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yaohui, registered in a military household in Linwu County, Guiyang Subprefecture, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Junna, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sigang (an Imperial University student), his grandfather Wenxiang (an Instructor), his father Mingdong (an Assistant Magistrate), and his mother née Chen; both parents were living, his elder brother was Yaoxun, and his wife was née Luo. He placed forty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Ci, registered in a civilian household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and originally from Guangde Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Bozhi, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Qingxiu, his father Li, and his mother née Chen; only his father was living, his younger brothers were Tianni and Tianyin, and he married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed sixty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wenbing, registered in a civilian household in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Daochong, he ranked eighth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Renwen, his grandfather Weixian, his father Qinghuan, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Wenwei, Wenzhao, and Wendeng, and he married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed sixty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Yi, registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zicheng, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ke, his grandfather Xin, his father Lin, and his mother née Tang; only his mother was living, his younger brother was Xin, and he married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.
