translation_en:
Shen Huan [?] (沈𤩽), courtesy name Bangzhong, was registered in an artisan household in the Wugong Left Guard and was originally from Deqing County, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyi, his grandfather Quan, and his father Mi; his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Shan, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Jie (蔡結), courtesy name Guoning, was registered in a military household in Hanyang County, Hanyang Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirtieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather Mi was an assistant prefect; his father was Zhuang, and his mother was née Xiao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yan, Luan, Ji, Ju, and Cai; his younger brother was Ti. His wife was née Wu. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zi (徐梓), courtesy name Ruliang, was registered in a civilian household in Yuhang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Jin, and his father Han, an Imperial University student; his mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhang, Yu, and Qi, and his wife was née Shao. He ranked eighty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Liang (石梁), courtesy name Shisheng, was registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Die, his grandfather Yilong, and his father Yuchou; his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Gong, Ying, Gui, and Bai, and his wife was née Xie. He ranked sixty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

卜大順〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣，匠籍，府學增廣生，治書經，字達夫，行四，年二十八，十二月初七日生〕。曾祖顥，祖周，父宗洛〔監生，贈奉直大夫、刑部員外郎〕，前母周氏〔贈宜人〕，母賀氏〔封太宜人〕。慈侍下，兄大同〔福建按察司副使〕、大有〔知縣〕、大觀，娶楊氏，繼娶顧氏。浙江鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百二十一名。

苗日科〔貫山西太原府石州寧鄉縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字淑四，行二，年三十二，十一月二十二日生〕。曾祖威，祖志廣，父希周〔監生〕，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄登，弟種、秩，娶王氏。山西鄉試第五十五名，會試第六十八名。

楊君璽〔貫彭城衛，軍籍，山東文登縣人，國子生，治詩經，字廷信，行一，年三十五，二月初三日生〕。曾祖能，祖逵，父鸞，母韓氏，繼母馮氏、孫氏。具慶下，弟君璧，娶徐氏，繼娶方氏、王氏。順天府鄉試第六十名，會試第二百三十七名。
translation_en:
Jiang Wanren, registered in an artisan household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruodu, he was third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minyi, his grandfather Fuheng, his father Chao, and his mother née Wei; his father alone was living. His elder brothers were Yan, a Sacrificial Official, and Wei; his younger brothers were Wanjie, Wancheng, Wanqing, Wanxiu, Wanyou, Wanyu, Wanxiu (萬秀), and Wanbo. He married a woman née Chen and placed sixty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 342nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Dashun, registered in an artisan household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Dafu, he was fourth in birth order, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Zhou, and his father Zongluo, an Imperial University student posthumously awarded the titles Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father's former wife, née Zhou, was posthumously awarded the title Lady of Suitability, and his mother, née He, was granted the title Senior Lady of Suitability. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Datong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner in Fujian, Dayou, a County Magistrate, and Daguan. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Gu; he placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Miao Rike, registered in a military household in Ningxiang County, Shizhou Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shusi, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei, his grandfather Zhiguang, his father Xizhou, an Imperial University student, and his mother née Yang; his mother alone was living. His elder brother was Deng, and his younger brothers were Zhong and Zhi. He married a woman née Wang and placed fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Junxi, registered in a military household of Pengcheng Guard and a native of Wendeng County, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingxin, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng, his grandfather Kui, his father Luan, his mother née Han, and his successive stepmothers née Feng and née Sun; both parents were living. His younger brother was Junbi. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently women née Fang and née Wang; he placed sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
董世彦〔貫河南開封府鈞州，民籍，國子生，治書經，字子才，行一，年二十七，四月初一日生〕。曾祖敬〔知縣〕，祖琇〔驛丞〕，父效賢〔州吏目〕，嫡母劉氏，繼母王氏，生母孔氏。具慶下，娶陳氏。河南鄉試第二十一名，會試第一百六十六名。

程熟〔貫直隸大名府開州，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字伯生，行一，年三十四，九月二十八日生〕。曾祖鑑〔山西按察使〕，祖宣仁，父萬殊〔知縣〕，母張氏。具慶下，弟燾、照〔監生〕，娶馬氏。順天府鄉試第九十一名，會試第一百三十四名。

莫抑〔貫廣西柳州府柳城縣，民籍，馬平縣人，國子生，治詩經，字允升，行一，年四十，十月初八日生〕。曾祖愚〔知縣〕，祖汝能〔知縣〕，父大德〔知縣〕，母秦氏。具慶下，弟揜、援、抗，娶趙氏，繼娶王氏。廣西鄉試第三十八名，會試第一百四十四名。

曾廷芝〔貫湖廣漢陽府漢陽縣，民籍，江西廬陵縣人，國子生，治詩經，字子芳，行二，年三十八，四月十九日生〕。曾祖處志，祖紹泂，父貴，母羅氏。慈侍下，兄廷選，娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第四十七名，會試第二百六十九名。
translation_en:
Dong Shiyan, registered in a civilian household in Jun Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zicai; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jing was a District Magistrate; his grandfather Xiu was a Station Master; and his father Xiaoxian was a subprefectural Clerk. His father's principal wife was Lady Liu, his stepmother was Lady Wang, and his birth mother was Lady Kong. Both parents were living. He married Lady Chen. He placed twenty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shu, registered in a military household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bosheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jian was Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi; his grandfather was Xuanren; his father Wanshu was a District Magistrate; and his mother was Lady Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tao and Zhao, the latter a student of the Imperial University. He married Lady Ma. He placed ninety-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Yi, registered in a civilian household in Liucheng County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, and a native of Maping County, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yunsheng; he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yu, grandfather Runeng, and father Dade were all District Magistrates; his mother was Lady Qin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yan, Yuan, and Kang. He married Lady Zhao and subsequently Lady Wang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Tingzhi, registered in a civilian household in Hanyang County, Hanyang Prefecture, Huguang, and a native of Luling County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zifang; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chuzhi, his grandfather was Shaojiong, his father was Gui, and his mother was Lady Luo. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Tingxuan. He married Lady Zhang. He placed forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

周斯盛〔貫陝西慶陽府寧州民籍，國子生，治書經，字子才，行一，年二十九，十一月十三日生〕。曾祖謙〔主簿，贈奉直大夫、南京戶部員外郎〕，祖達〔奉直大夫、南京戶部員外郎〕，父習吉，母劉氏。具慶下，弟斯美、斯興、斯明、斯來、斯謨、斯永、斯猷、斯善、斯孝，娶呂氏。陝西鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百二名。

潘子霓〔貫山東濟南府羣牧所軍籍，山西蔚州人，府學生，治詩經，字望甫，行三，年二十九，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖普海，祖鐸，父相，母趙氏。具慶下，兄子雨〔貢士〕、子震，娶李氏。山東鄉試第十六名，會試第一百五十八名。
translation_en:
Zhu Zhen, registered in a civilian household in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an附attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruzhong; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shiyi, his grandfather Yushan, his father Wenkui, and his mother née Yao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Biao and Zuo, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhi, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Sishang; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Heng, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather Wenbin was posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of War; and his father Xu was a Prefect. His mother, née Yu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren), and his stepmother, née Weng, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother was Yu, his younger brothers were Xi and Zhong, and his wife was née Fang. He ranked seventy-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Sisheng, registered in a civilian household in Ningzhou, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zicai; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Qian was a Registrar, posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Upright Service and the office of Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. His grandfather Da held that rank and office. His father was Xiji, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Simei, Sixing, Siming, Silai, Simo, Siyong, Siyou, Sishan, and Sixiao; his wife was née Lü. He ranked fifty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Zini, registered in a military household at the Qunmu Office in Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was originally from Yuzhou, Shanxi. He was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wangfu; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Puhai, his grandfather Duo, his father Xiang, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ziyu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Zizhen; his wife was née Li. He ranked sixteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉曰材〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字汝成，行十，年三十一，九月初四日生〕。曾祖伯韶，祖廷璋，父仕沃，母何氏。具慶下，弟曰禎，娶楊氏。江西鄉試第四十九名，會試第一百九十八名。

劉泉〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣，民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字漸甫，行一，年四十一，七月初六日生〕。曾祖桓，祖煊，父寅，母沈氏。永感下，弟汞、永、泶，娶蔣氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十四名，會試第二百七十三名。

translation_en:
Huang Ji, registered in Changyuan County, Kai Department, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zixiu, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Zhao, his father Cheng, and his mother née Song; his parents and grandparents were living, his elder brother was Fan, his younger brother Jia, and his wife née Mao; he placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yuecai, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rucheng, he ranked tenth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Boshao, his grandfather Tingzhang, his father Shiwo, and his mother née He; both parents were living, his younger brother was Yuezhen, and his wife was née Yang; he placed forty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Quan, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Jianfu, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged forty-one, born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Xuan, his father Yin, and his mother née Shen; both parents were deceased, his younger brothers were Gong, Yong, and Xue [?], and his wife was née Jiang; he placed 134th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Peng, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Runan, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Jiang, his father Zongcheng, and his mother née Lu; both parents were living, his elder brother was Qi, and his wife was née Jiang; he placed thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

王察言〔貫山東東昌府濮州朝城縣，民籍，山西馬邑縣人，縣學生，治詩經，字師舜，行一，年三十七，二月初九日生〕。曾祖玘，祖雄〔贈監察御史〕，父應〔監察御史〕，嫡母趙氏〔封孺人〕，生母袁氏。具慶下，弟容言〔監生〕，娶尹氏。山東鄉試第十二名，會試第二百二十九名。

向淇〔貫湖廣辰州府沅陵縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字子瞻，行三，年四十一，九月十八日生〕。曾祖和宗，祖志昱〔省祭官〕，父盈，母張氏，繼母瞿氏。具慶下，兄濬、澤，弟灝、淳、沔、治，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第七十一名，會試第六十四名。

translation_en:
Yin Shilong, courtesy name Jianqing, was registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked thirty-fourth in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Jian, his father Shen, and his mother née Gu; his mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Shirong, Shiliang, Shiyuan, and Shiying, and his wife was née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chayan, courtesy name Shishun, was registered in Chaocheng County, Pu Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household, and was a native of Mayi County, Shanxi. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather Xiong was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor, and his father Ying was an Investigating Censor. His legal mother was née Zhao, granted the title Lady of Goodness (ruren), and his birth mother was née Yuan; both parents were living. His younger brother Rongyan was an Imperial University student, and his wife was née Yin. He placed twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Qi, courtesy name Zizhan, was registered in Yuanling County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hezong; his grandfather Zhiyu was a Sacrificial Attendant; his father was Ying, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Qu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jun and Ze, his younger brothers Hao, Chun, Mian, and Zhi, and his wife was née Liu. He placed seventy-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Jimin, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in Dingxing County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Shouzheng was an Assistant Instructor, his grandfather Zongwu a subprefectural Clerk, his father Heng, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Baomin, his younger brothers Fumin and Zemin, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Ru 朱茹, courtesy name Yihui, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked tenth in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ziming, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Huang, posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; his father was Zigong, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Guo, held the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jia, Chai, Zao (Surveillance Vice Commissioner), Di, Kui, Ying, Ru [?—the same name as the candidate], E, Ai, and Jin; his younger brother was Qin. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Zhou 盛周, courtesy name Wenyu, was registered in an artisan household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Hong, his father Song, and his mother née Shen. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Wu. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jiuyi 張九一, courtesy name Zhufu, was registered in a civilian household in Xincai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixteenth in his family and was twenty-one years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Huai, a Police Chief; his grandfather was Jian, a student of the Imperial University; his father was Shen; and his mother was née Dai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiuxi, Jiude, Jiushao, Jiujing, Jiurong, and Jiugao; his younger brothers were Jiuer and Jiusan. He married a woman née Wang. He placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 361st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Weifan 沈維藩, courtesy name Yueqing, was registered in a military household of Dingzhou Guard in the directly administered metropolitan territory and was a native of Dehua County, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Jian, and his father Wei, a Prefectural School Professor. His legal mother was née Gao, and his birth mother was née Song. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Weining and Weiping. He married a woman née Yin and subsequently married women née Liu and née Zhang. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Jiabin was registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yuxian and ranked first among his brothers. He was aged thirty-two [?; the transcription has an additional 月, “month”] and was born on the seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jinwen; his grandfather, Ding, was a county-school instructor; his father was Shunchen, and his mother was née Zhou. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yongbin and Dabin, and his wife was née Xu. He placed nineteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Qiao was registered in a military household in Guangji County, Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ziqian and ranked first among his brothers. He was aged thirty-eight and was born on the fourteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Jinggui, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, Ying, was a district magistrate; his father was Wanshan, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Gao, and his wife was née Kou. He placed forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Shi was registered in a military household of Qingyang Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Yushe County, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Borun and ranked first among his brothers. He was aged twenty-nine and was born on the twenty-third day of the third month. His great-grandfather was San; his grandfather was Gang; his father was Qin. His father’s former wives were née Ma and née Han, and his mother was née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Yang. He placed thirteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Ruchun was registered in an officer household of the Luoyang Central Escort Guard, Henan, and was a native of Yidu County, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Hefu and ranked second among his brothers. He was aged twenty-nine and was born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Hou, and grandfather, Sheng, were both vice commanders; his father, Xiu, was a vice prefect, and his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother, Ruyu, was a vice commander, and his younger brother, Ruzhang, was a tribute scholar who had passed the Metropolitan Examination. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jin Yan, courtesy name Shangbin, was registered in a military household in Qianshan County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Pujing, his grandfather Guangying, his father Xie, and his mother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qiao and Jin, and his wife was née Chen. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jiushao, courtesy name Chengfu, was registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Zi, his father Zongdao, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiuxia, Jiufan, and Jiuling. His wife was née Xu; he subsequently married another woman née Xu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Fei, courtesy name Yinzhou, was registered in a civilian household in Jian'an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. An added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Record of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ang, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Chong, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his father was Dun, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tang, his younger brothers were Bo and Qu, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed sixteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yu, courtesy name Jichun, was registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhun, his grandfather Wentong, his father Zonghai, and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhen, a Sacrificial Attendant (shengjiguan), and Jie; his wife was née Zhang. He placed seventeenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qin Keda, registered in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongxiu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Fu, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Governance and Vice Prefect of Fengyang Prefecture; and his father was E, a Chief Administrator [preceding character illegible], granted the additional privilege of wearing the dress of an illegible rank. His mother, née Xie, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother, née He, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kejiu, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Keshang, Kejian, Keguan, and Keji. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Xing. He placed twentieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 325th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dongbo, registered in Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mengqing; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, a prefectural Administrative Clerk; his grandfather was Yingchen, a subprefectural Vice Magistrate; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Wen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Dongsheng and Dongzuo, and his younger brothers were Dongtiao and Dongshen. He married a woman née Jin. He placed twenty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Peng belonged to a military household registered with the Battalion of Pingding Subprefecture, Shanxi, and was a native of Datong County, Datong Prefecture. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zizhuan; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu; his grandfather was Wenyuan, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Tingzhao, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Wei. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was He. He married a woman née Bai and subsequently women née Zhao, An, and Quan. He placed twenty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Wenkui, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xuanming; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather was Yingyou, a prefectural Registrar; his father was Bangxian; and his mother was née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenwan, and his younger brother was Wenbi. He married a woman née Sun. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Wenrong, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Guohua; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Zao; his father was Yi; his mother was née Xi, and his stepmother née Jin. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Wenming and Wenru. He married a woman née Pan and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Weiqing, registered in a military household of Dingliao Left Guard in Liaodong and originating from Huang County, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Xiangzhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather was Zheng; his father was Xin, and his mother née Xie. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Weichen. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 384th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Zhu, registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Guozhen; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Pei; his father was Dezhao, an Assistant Magistrate of a department; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Bang. He married a woman née Shen. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Jiufeng, registered in a military household of Xingzhou Rear Garrison Guard in Zhili and originating from Luling County, Jiangxi, was a Sanhe County school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Shoufu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Rui, an Assistant Prefect; his father was Xuan, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief. His father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Zhao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Jiucheng, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort; his younger brothers were Jiuxi, Jiusi, Jiuxu, Jiugao, and Jiuguan. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently another woman née Liu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

管嘉福〔貫山東萊州府膠州高密縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字正甫，行二，年四十二，二月初七日生〕。曾祖進，祖惠，父九雲〔學正〕，母王氏。嚴侍下，兄嘉禎〔太常寺博士〕，弟嘉猷、嘉言、嘉祥、嘉謨、嘉謀、嘉德、嘉行、嘉樂，娶李氏，繼娶呂氏。山東鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百九十一名。

李鳳〔貫廣東廣州府番禺縣民籍，江西南康縣人，縣學附學生，治詩經，字鳴岡，行三，年三十五，二月初三日生〕。曾祖源，祖棠，父賢〔八品散官〕，母羅氏。永感下，兄鸞〔戶部主事〕、鶚，娶黃氏。廣東鄉試第四十八名，會試第三百十二名。

translation_en:
Li Boyu, courtesy name Zaichun, was registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian; he was an attached student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Ying, his father Xiong, and his mother née Chen; both parents were living; his elder brother was Boxiang and his younger brothers were Boyu (伯愚), Bolu, Bochao, and Boshi; he married a woman née Wang and placed fortieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guan Jiafu, courtesy name Zhengfu, was registered in a civilian household in Gaomi County, Jiaozhou, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong; he was a student of the Imperial University, specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged forty-two, born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Hui, his father Jiuyun, a School Instructor, and his mother née Wang; his father alone was living; his elder brother was Jiazhen, an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and his younger brothers were Jiayou, Jiayan, Jiaxiang, Jiamo, Jiamou, Jiade, Jiaxing, and Jiale; he married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Lü, and placed thirty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Feng, courtesy name Minggang, was registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a native of Nankang County, Jiangxi; he was an attached student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Tang, his father Xian, who held an eighth-rank prestige title, and his mother née Luo; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Luan, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and E; he married a woman née Huang and placed forty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jia, courtesy name Huixian, was registered in a military household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was an added-quota student of the prefectural school, specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Zhe, a tribute student, his father Wanchun, and his mother née Gong; his mother alone was living; his younger brothers were Bing, Geng, and Ren; he married a woman née Jiang and placed eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zonghui, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Binzhi; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Ding, his father Gang, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zongmo, and his wife was née Liao. He placed thirtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Daihua, registered in a civilian household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wen, his grandfather Jian, and his father Tianmin, who held an honorary title for longevity. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Daiyuan, and his wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Daozhi, registered in a civilian household in Ding Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Hong, his father Sen, a District Magistrate, and his mother née Dong. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Daogong, Daozheng, and Daoping; his younger brothers were Daoming and Daozhong. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qiaogui, registered in a salt-producing household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Songs. His courtesy name was Xingjie; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tongqian, his grandfather Jizhang, and his father Wenxi. His father's former wife was née Cai, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiaochun and Qiaosong, and his younger brother was Qiaozi. His wife was née Lai. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Chun, courtesy name Zhongpang, was registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ben; his grandfather was Xian, an honorary Official for Longevity; and his father was Shirong, a Registrar. His father’s former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Kong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhan, Zhi, Shu, and Zhu. His wife was née Zhou. He placed forty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 311th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tinglong, courtesy name Dehua, was registered in a military household in Xiangyin County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twentieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Daoming, a Subprefectural Judge; and his father was Peng. His mother was née Su. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingzuo. His wife was née Song. He placed thirty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Quan, courtesy name Yuanxue, was registered with the Sichuan Ceremonial Guard Office and was a native of Wenjiang County, Chengdu Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-eight, and born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhicong; his grandfather was Su; and his father was Yongsheng. His mother was née Zou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jin, and his younger brothers were Jie, She, Qian, Qi, and He. His wife was née Shen; he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed forty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Jinghe, courtesy name Shuxuan, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yongqing; his grandfather was Zheng; and his father was Xianrong. His father’s former wife and his mother were both née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jingxing and Jingming. His wife was née Gui. He placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yinshi, courtesy name Yuzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Sheng, held the honorary title of Official for Longevity; his father, Zhao, was a Magistrate; and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yinbin, and his younger brothers were Yinliang, Yinqi, Yinfa, Yinkuan, Yinshi (寅仕), Yinhao, Yinchen, and Yincai. His wife was née Lu. He ranked twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xing, courtesy name Zhiti, was registered in a civilian household in Boye County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather, Tingzhang, was a Sacrificial Official (shengjiguan); his father, Luan, was a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhou and Hua, and his wife was née Chen. He ranked 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Qimeng, courtesy name Yangzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Gui, was an Investigating Censor posthumously granted the title of Minister. His grandfather, Chun, was Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites, concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy, administering the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous name was Wenjian. His father, Yannian, was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites, and his mother, née Deng, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qizong, a Prefect, and Qidong, a Secretary; his younger brothers were Qijing, an Imperial University student, and Qijiang. His wife was née Yang, and his subsequent wife was née Mou. He ranked eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 370th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yaofeng, courtesy name Shuhua, was registered in a civilian household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Feng, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his grandfather was Zhidao; his father was Zhi; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zhang, and he was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Liu. He ranked sixty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Ruzheng, registered in a civilian household in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a department school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yangzhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Yi, his father Rui, and his mother née Li; both parents were living, and his wife was née Pan. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lin, registered in a military household in Henan Guard, Henan, and a native of Tongcheng County in Zhili, was an additional student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zixiang, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Xian, his father Tang, and his mother née Yang; his grandparents and parents were living, his elder brother was Qi, his younger brothers were Luan and Feng, and his wife was née Wen. He placed seventy-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Liang, registered in a civilian household in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yuchen, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Si, an honorary official; his grandfather was Chang, his father Yanhong, his mother née Zhu, and his stepmother née Zhang; both parents were living, his younger brother was Yi, and his wife was née Liu. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Shifang, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zishi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Sirong, his father Li, his mother née He, and his stepmother née Hao; his grandparents and parents were living, his younger brother was Lianfang, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and three hundred and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhen Jing, courtesy name Ziyi, was registered in a military household of the Thousand-household Office of Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a native of Lan County, Kelan Subprefecture. A subprefectural government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuxiang; his grandfather, Yong, held the conferred title of Secretariat Drafter; his father, Chengde, was Supervising Secretary in the Nanjing Office of Scrutiny for War; and his mother, née Ma, held the conferred title of Lady (Ruren). His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Min, Xiao, Mei, and Fu, and his wife was née Cao. He placed forty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Youwang, courtesy name Sidao, was registered in a civilian household of Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Tai; and his father, Song. His father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Youpeng, Youkun, and You'e, and his wife was née Fang. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Zhongyi, courtesy name Lüdao, was registered in an artisan household of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao; his grandfather, Jiang; his father, Zonggui; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living, and his wife was née Li. He placed forty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Zengwei, courtesy name Yiguan, was registered in a civilian household of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather, Gang; his father, Wenzao; and his mother, née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zengde, and his younger brothers were Zengxue, Zengyue, Zengxiao, Zengdi, Zengxing, and Zengsi. His wife was née Zhu. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

穆寧中〔貫府軍前衛官籍，直隸永平府山海衛人，國子生，治易經，字允執，行一，年三十四，十一月二十九日生〕。曾祖聚，祖清，父謙，前母郭氏、石氏，母劉氏，繼母趙氏。慈侍下，弟恕，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第八十四名，會試第二百七十二名。

葛大紀〔貫直隸潼關衛旗籍，陝西商州人，國子生，治書經，字伯理，行二，年二十七，十一月十八日生〕。曾祖忠〔總旗〕，祖亮〔總旗〕，父蔓，母李氏。具慶下，兄大綱，娶張氏。陝西鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百六十三名。
translation_en:
Zhang Cunyi 張存義, courtesy name Yifu, was registered in a civilian household in Jian’an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liu; his grandfather, Wenzhen; his father, Xiang; and his mother, née Zhuo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Cunren, and his younger brothers were Cunli, Cunzhi, and Cunxin. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed eighty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Tongwen 錢同文, courtesy name Daxing, was registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather, Pu; his father, Ruli; and his mother, née Zhu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Tongsheng, Tongchun, and Tongfang. He married a woman née Fei. He placed thirty-second in both the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

Mu Ningzhong 穆寧中, courtesy name Yunzhi, was registered in a military officer household of the Fujun Front Guard and was a native of Shanhai Guard, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather, Qing; and his father, Qian. His father’s former wives were née Guo and née Shi; his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Zhao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Shu. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Daji 葛大紀, courtesy name Boli, was registered in a military banner household of Tongguan Guard in the directly administered region and was a native of Shangzhou, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhong and grandfather Liang were both company commanders; his father was Man, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dagang. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ling Ru, registered in the civilian-artisan category in Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhenqing, he was third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhenfang, his grandfather Qi, his father Ke, and his mother née Zhou; his grandparents and parents were living, his elder brothers were Ren and Yi, his younger brother was Ren (任), and his wife was née Pan; he placed 124th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Sen, registered as a civilian in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Maoshou, he was third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanjing, his grandfather Kun (an honorary official honored for longevity), his father Han (a School Instructor), and his mother née Liu; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Bang (an Instructor in Yin-yang Studies) and Mao, and his wife was née Zheng; he placed 85th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 75th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Shanmu, registered as a civilian in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, directly administered territory, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zimei, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Long, his grandfather Shen, his father Xi, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Shansong, Shanliang, Shanbai, Shanfeng, and Shangui, and he married a woman née Fang and subsequently a woman née Liu; he placed 98th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 343rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Gui, registered in the military category in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zizhang, he was fifth in birth order, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingshun, his grandfather Lun, his father Deguang, his mother née Zhou, and his stepmother née Fu; both parents were living, his elder brother was Tang, his younger brothers were Jie, Shi, Yuan, Tai, Chi, and Bi, and his wife was née Wang; he placed 42nd in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Yanmin, registered in a civilian household in Neiqiu County, Shunde Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziwei; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengxiang, a prefectural Record Keeper; his grandfather was Jing; and his father was Zongzhou, a County Magistrate. His mother, née Ning, was still living; his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Xianmin, Junmin, and Xiumin, and his younger brother was Huimin. He married a woman née Yan. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Long, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Qianfu; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunchong, a County Registrar; his grandfather was Gang, a County Clerk posthumously granted the rank of Gentleman of Literary Service; and his father was Qi, a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His mother, née Min, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brother Conglong was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Xu. He placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Qianshou, registered in a military household in Yingcheng County, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yiren; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiqing; his grandfather was Zhao; his father was Zixin; and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jieshou, Pengshou, Chunshou, Qiaoshou, and Yanshou, and his younger brother was Kunshou. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Zhong, registered in a military household in Weinan County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruqi; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Cong; his father was Shouyang; his mother was née Ma; and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were recorded as living. His elder brother was Yu. He married a woman née Guo. He placed forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Xueyan 張學顏, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in Feixiang County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shao, a Police Chief; his grandfather was Yue, an Assistant Instructor; and his father was Yingqi, a Prefectural Subprefect. His mother was née Song, and his stepmother née Tao. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Xueyin, and his wife was née Liu. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bosheng 李伯生, courtesy name Ziyuan, was registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a military household. An added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benliang, his grandfather Ying, and his father Maosong; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhaosheng, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zuofu 黃作孚, courtesy name Rucong, was registered in Jimo County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Zhao, and his father Zheng; his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zuosu, and his younger brothers were Zuozhe, Zuosheng, and Zuolin. His wife was née Sun. He placed seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 347th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Qixun 蕭奇勳, courtesy name Maojian, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Renfu, and his father Gui, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Cai, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. The annotation lists his elder brother as Qiying and his younger brothers as Qilie, Qice, Qizhao, Qiyue, Qijie, Qiye, Qiyi, Qiyao, Qitun, Qitao, Qijie [name repeated in the text], and Qican. His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Conglong, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Jiading County, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Boyun, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Xiang, was a subprefectural Clerk; his father, Zhixue, was an Assistant Subprefect; and his mother was née Qian. His parents and grandparents were living; his younger brothers were Qilong and Yinglong, and his wife was née Yu. He ranked one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 324th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Yingguang, registered in a military household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zishi, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Fei, was posthumously granted the title of Vice Commander of a Military Police Office on account of his son Jin; his grandfather, Jin, held that office; his father was Qian, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased; his elder brother was Yingkui, and he married a woman née Xin and subsequently a woman née Su. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Hu, registered in a civilian household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county government student who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhouzhen, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Mengxun; his grandfather, Youxiang; his father, Zixiong; his mother, née Guo; and his stepmother, née Xu. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Sen and Zan, and his wife was née Cai. He ranked ninetieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Shixue, registered in a military household of Henan Guard in Henan, was a prefectural government student who specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Minzhi, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Kuang; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living; his younger brother was Shisheng, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 396th in the Metropolitan Examination.

貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣民籍　國子生

曾祖佐　祖懋〔壽官〕　父澄〔訓導〕　前母盧氏　母張氏
具慶下　兄宗夏　宗孔　宗堯　宗孟　弟宗禹　宗湯　宗文　宗武　娶李氏
山西鄉試第三十四名　會試第三百九十三名
punctuated:
陳珊〔貫貴州銅仁府銅仁司民籍，四川富順縣人，國子生，治詩經，字鳴仲，行一，年四十四，三月三十日生〕。曾祖中正，祖綺〔倉副使〕，父時謨〔縣丞〕，母熊氏。具慶下，弟瑚〔驛丞〕、珮、璋，娶孫氏。貴州鄉試第二名，會試第三百四名。

黃乾行〔貫福建福寧州軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字叔健，行十，年三十九，二月初九日生〕。曾祖袞，祖發，父子厚〔訓導〕，前母林氏，母雷氏。永感下，兄乾清、乾德〔知縣〕，弟乾道，娶王氏。福建鄉試第八十七名，會試第二百九十七名。

凌邦奇〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字正伯，行一，年四十一，十一月二十六日生〕。曾祖晟，祖亮，父艮，前母金氏，母俞氏，繼母浦氏。永感下，弟邦彥，娶戈氏。應天府鄉試第八十名，會試第七十九名。

王宗舜〔貫山西平陽府解州聞喜縣軍籍，縣學生，治春秋，字用中，行五，年三十五，十二月二十二日生〕。曾祖佐，祖懋〔壽官〕，父澄〔訓導〕，前母盧氏，母張氏。具慶下，兄宗夏、宗孔、宗堯、宗孟，弟宗禹、宗湯、宗文、宗武，娶李氏。山西鄉試第三十四名，會試第三百九十三名。
translation_en:
Chen Shan, courtesy name Mingzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Tongren Si, Tongren Prefecture, Guizhou, and was a native of Fushun County, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in birth order and was forty-four years old, born on the thirtieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongzheng; his grandfather, Qi, was a Granary Vice Commissioner; and his father, Shimo, was an Assistant Magistrate. His mother was née Xiong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hu, a Station Master, Pei, and Zhang. His wife was née Sun. He placed second in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Qianxing, courtesy name Shujian, was registered in a military household in Funing Subprefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked tenth in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gun; his grandfather, Fa; and his father, Zihou, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Lei. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qianqing and Qiande, the latter a Magistrate; his younger brother was Qiandao. His wife was née Wang. He placed eighty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ling Bangqi, courtesy name Zhengbo, was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in birth order and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Liang; and his father, Gen. His father's former wife was née Jin, his mother was née Yu, and his stepmother was née Pu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Bangyan. His wife was née Ge. He placed eightieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongshun, courtesy name Yongzhong, was registered in a military household in Wenxi County, Jie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fifth in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuo; his grandfather, Mao, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; and his father, Cheng, was an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zongxia, Zongkong, Zongyao, and Zongmeng; his younger brothers were Zongyu, Zongtang, Zongwen, and Zongwu. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 393rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

歸大道〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字懋庸，行二，年三十，二月二十四日生〕。曾祖璣，祖椿，父俸，母張氏。具慶下，兄大德，弟大中、大有、大賓，娶陳氏。順天府鄉試第七十四名，會試第三百七十二名。

錢邦偁〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄水縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字叔美，行一，年四十一，九月初十日生〕。曾祖俊，祖重器〔知縣〕，父貢〔府同知〕，母吳氏。慈侍下，弟邦似、邦伊、邦存，娶周氏。湖廣鄉試第四十三名，會試第三百五名。

葉期遠〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字士毅，行一，年四十二，二月初六日生〕。曾祖聰，祖諫，父元浩，母丘氏，繼母鄭氏。慈侍下，弟期逮、期邁、期暹、期逢，娶徐氏，繼娶柳氏。順天府鄉試第六名，會試第二百二十八名。

何棨〔貫順天府涿州民籍，國子生，治詩經，字信卿，行三，年三十三，十月二十五日生〕。曾祖順，祖仲良，父溥，母謝氏。慈侍下，兄相、楫，弟檠，娶呂氏。順天府鄉試第一百十四名，會試第二百九十名。
translation_en:
Gui Dadao, of civilian household registration in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Maoyong, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged 30, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Chun, his father Feng, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living; his elder brother was Dade and his younger brothers Dazhong, Dayou, and Dabin; his wife was née Chen; he placed seventy-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 372nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Bangcheng, of military household registration in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shumei, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged 41, born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Chongqi, a District Magistrate, his father Gong, a Vice Prefect, and his mother née Wu; his mother alone was living; his younger brothers were Bangsi, Bangyi, and Bangcun; his wife was née Zhou; he placed forty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 305th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Qiyuan, of civilian household registration in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shiyi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged 42, born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Jian, his father Yuanhao, his mother née Qiu, and his stepmother née Zheng; his father was deceased and his mother or stepmother was living; his younger brothers were Qidai, Qimai, Qixian, and Qifeng; his first wife was née Xu and his subsequent wife née Liu; he placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Qi, of civilian household registration in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Songs; his courtesy name was Xinqing, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged 33, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Zhongliang, his father Pu, and his mother née Xie; his mother alone was living; his elder brothers were Xiang and Ji and his younger brother Qing; his wife was née Lü; he placed 114th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十二年進士登科錄

punctuated:
華秉中〔貫直隸松江府上海縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字正夫，行一，年三十五，九月十三日生〕。曾祖瑞，祖昱，父鯨，母潘氏。具慶下，弟秉道、秉良、秉才，娶王氏，繼娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第八十八名，會試第一百四十四名。

郭嵩〔貫湖廣承天府潜江縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字叔中，行三，年三十五，六月十六日生〕。曾祖允榮，祖璡，父世朝〔監生〕，母柴氏。慈侍下，兄嵒〔監生〕、岱、岺，弟嶠、岳、岑，娶蔣氏。湖廣鄉試第五十名，會試第一百二十九名。

李佩〔貫陝西漢中府南鄭縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字子玉，行一，年四十二，十一月初三日生〕。曾祖八，祖成，父志和，嫡母尚氏，生母張氏。慈侍下，娶湯氏。陝西鄉試第五十二名，會試第一百九十九名。

王惟寧〔貫陝西西安府興平縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子靜，行一，年三十二，三月十一日生〕。曾祖恭政，祖文達，父官，嫡母趙氏，生母韓氏。具慶下，弟惟幾，娶李氏，繼娶張氏。陝西鄉試第四十七名，會試第一百八十三名。
translation_en:
Hua Bingzhong, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhengfu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui, his grandfather Yu, his father Jing, and his mother née Pan; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Bingdao, Bingliang, and Bingcai, and he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhu; he placed eighty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Song, registered in Qianjiang County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shuzhong, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunrong, his grandfather Jin, his father Shichao (a student of the Directorate of Education), and his mother née Chai; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brothers were Yan (a student of the Directorate of Education), Dai, and Ling, and his younger brothers were Jiao, Yue, and Cen; he married a woman née Jiang and placed fiftieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Pei, registered in Nanzheng County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was forty-two years old, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ba, his grandfather Cheng, his father Zhihe, his legal mother née Shang, and his birth mother née Zhang; his father was deceased and his mother living, he married a woman née Tang, and he placed fifty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Weining, registered in Xingping County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zijing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongzheng, his grandfather Wenda, his father Guan, his legal mother née Zhao, and his birth mother née Han; both parents were living, his younger brother was Weiji, and he married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhang; he placed forty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Gongyong, registered in Cheng’an County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jinchen; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Lun, his father Long, and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Chaoyong, Junyong, and Tingyong; his wife was née Li. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 355th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Wan, registered in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zixiu; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was forty-two years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yizhong, a prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather was Chong, and his father Zhen. His father’s former wife was née Tang, and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Rong, an annual tribute student, Cai, Bin, Huan, and Chong; his wife was née Tong. He placed forty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chao Dongwu, registered in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shutai; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-two years old, born on the eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather Delong held the honorary title of Examining Editor of the Hanlin Academy; and his father Li was an Examining Editor of the Hanlin Academy. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his stepmother, also née Zhang, was granted the same title. His family status was recorded as having grandparents and parents living. His elder brothers were Dongzhou and Dongshan; his younger brothers were Dongjiao, Donglu, Dongguo, Dongdu, and Dongqi. His wife was née Cheng. He placed seventy-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Kui belonged to a military household registered in Guangning Central Guard, Liaodong, and was a native of Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Guoxiang; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Zhong, his father Cheng, and his mother née Tang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Ping; his younger brothers were Bi and Shi. His wife was née Zhu. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 386th in the Metropolitan Examination.
