translation_en:
Bian Xi 邊傒, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in an official household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Yong was a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, posthumously granted the title of right assistant censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his grandfather Yong 鏞 was right vice minister of Justice at Nanjing; his father Xinxue was a surveillance vice commissioner; and his mother, née Yang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Huang, a transport commissioner; Ying, a prefect; Qiao, a department magistrate; Bo, an administrative assistant in Yingtian Prefecture; Zhong, a government student; Cheng, an administrator; Zhou, a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue; Shen, a department magistrate; Tan, a judge; Xi 傒, a student of the Directorate of Education [the same name as the candidate, ?]; and Xi 俙, a government student. His younger brothers Yi and Su were both students of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Feng. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bangkui 李邦魁, courtesy name Shiyuan, was registered in a military household in Gaomi County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Lin was a county vice magistrate; his grandfather was Shi; his father was Zhongling; his mother was née Guan; and his stepmothers were née Yi and née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Shan. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Jizu 宋繼祖, courtesy name Ruxiao, was registered in a civilian household at Madian Postal Relay Station, Zhongjiang County, Tongchuan Department, Sichuan, and was originally from Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. An additional student at the Hanzhou government school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Hai; his father was Tinggui; his mother was née Wu; and his stepmother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Guangzu, Xingzu, Yangzu, and Shengzu. He married a woman née Cai. He placed fifty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jiao 趙教, courtesy name Zixue, was registered in a civilian household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An instructor at the Dingzhou government school in Zhili specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the twenty-second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xun; his grandfather was Shiyong; his father was Shixiang; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zheng, and his younger brother's name is illegible (□). He married a woman née Liang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 345th in the Metropolitan Examination.

夏儒〔貫直隸鎮江府丹徒縣，軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字汝醇，行五，年三十八，九月十四日生〕。曾祖珪，祖珍，父鸞，母徐氏。永感下，兄偉、仁，弟僎、信、儲、寵、儀、宥、儼、閎、實，娶嚴氏。應天府鄉試第七十二名，會試第三百二十名。

徐浦〔貫福建建寧府浦城縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字伯源，行三，年三十，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖秉常，祖禋，父鳳，母葉氏。慈侍下，弟泓、洞，娶祖氏。福建鄉試第七十三名，會試第三百八十八名。
translation_en:
Liu Mingyang, registered in Yu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yingming. He ranked first among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fubao, his grandfather Jing, and his father Tingxi; his father's former wife was née Han, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Ji. His father alone was still living. His younger brothers were Mingzhu, Mingyin, and Mingqian, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 397th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Ming, registered in Jian’an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zishun. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-seven years old, and was born on the tenth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Mengxuan and grandfather Jun both held honorary official status conferred for longevity; his father Kai was a county school instructor, and his mother was née Shi. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Qing and Cui, his younger brother was Chang, and his wife was née Pan. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 360th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Ru, registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Ruchun. He ranked fifth among his brothers, was thirty-eight years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Zhen, his father Luan, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wei and Ren; his younger brothers were Zhuan, Xin, Chu, Chong, Yi, You, Yan, Hong, and Shi. His wife was née Yan. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Pu, registered in Pucheng County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Boyuan. He ranked third among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingchang, his grandfather Yin, his father Feng, and his mother née Ye. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Hong and Dong, and his wife was née Zu. He placed seventy-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 388th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Shimao, registered in Huguan County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Zhaoqing, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Qi, and his father Xu, a Sacrificial Attendant; his mother was née Xu, both parents were living, his younger brothers were Shixiu, Shixuan, Shiwang, Shijin, and Shijue, and his wife was née Xu; he placed twenty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Fang, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education, with the unclear wording “Jinxian Fan” [?] preceding his student status; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Yifu, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-one, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongjing, his grandfather Yuebang, his father Yi, and his mother née Wan; both parents were living, his wife was née Wan, and he placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shushen, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Sicheng, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the eleventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pengfei, his grandfather Yu, his father Ning, and his mother née Ren; his father alone was living, his elder brother was Shupan, his younger brother Shuyou, and his wife née Kong; he placed thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Jing, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county Confucian school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Junxi, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongheng, his grandfather Zizhan, his father Huan, and his mother née Luo; his mother alone was living, his elder brother was Jian, his younger brother Yao, and his wife née Chen; he placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Daxue, courtesy name Xizeng, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in the civilian register. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shizong; his grandfather, Mengjian; his father, Zhongzhang, a Post Station Master; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wenxue, Laixue, Youxue, and Minxue. He married a woman née Wu. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 358th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Pan, courtesy name Luzai, was registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in the civilian register. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, an Administration Vice Commissioner in Jiangxi, advanced to the rank of Grand Master of Palace; his grandfather was Lang; his father, Gao, selected for appointment as an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Yan. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuan, an Imperial University student, Han, Hui, Liu, and Hun. He married a woman née Cai and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zi, courtesy name Bolin, was registered in the military register of Qingzhou Left Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Zhucheng County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Zhen; his father, Chen; and his mother, née Dong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ru, Jin, Si, and Qian. He married a woman née Qi. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Rulin, courtesy name Shiwang, was registered in Yongfeng County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in the civilian register. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Danzhuo; his grandfather, Zongzhi; his father, Chaopu; and his mother, née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ruji and Rumei. He married a woman née Qiu and subsequently women née Song and née Wang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉祜〔貫山東萊州府掖縣匠籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字淑脩，行一，年二十八，正月十一日生〕。曾祖通，祖真，父廷珮〔省祭官〕，母官氏。具慶下，弟祚，娶徐氏。山東鄉試第三十六名，會試第二百五十五名。

劉以節〔貫廣東潮州府海陽縣民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字叔度，行一，年三十，四月二十二日生〕。曾祖錫，祖伯瑞，父璉，嫡母鄭氏，生母朱氏。慈侍下，娶盧氏。廣東鄉試第七十名，會試第二百六十六名。

徐大壯〔貫直隸大名府開州長垣縣民籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字子貞，行一，年三十九，八月初十日生〕。曾祖清，祖鸞，父昪，母黃氏。嚴侍下，弟大夏，娶李氏，繼娶王氏、侯氏。順天府鄉試第八十名，會試第三百七十四名。
translation_en:
Cui Kongxin, registered in a military household in Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jinming, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Yu, a Company Commander; his father was Dun; and his mother was née Yin. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Kongyuan and Kongzhao, and his younger brothers were Kongyang, Kongshi, Kongben, Kongfang, Kongqian, and Kongyao. His wife was née Shi. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 382nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Hu, registered in an artisan household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shuxiu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Zhen; his father was Tingpei, a Sacrificial Attendant; and his mother was née Guan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zuo, and his wife was née Xu. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yijie, registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shudu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xi; his grandfather was Borui; his father was Lian; his legal mother was née Zheng; and his birth mother was née Zhu. His mother alone was living. His wife was née Lu. He placed seventieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Dazhuang, registered in a civilian household in Changyuan County, Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zizhen, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Luan; his father was Bian; and his mother was née Huang. His father alone was living. His younger brother was Daxia. His wife was née Li, and his subsequent wives were née Wang and née Hou. He placed eightieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 374th in the Metropolitan Examination.

唐繼祿〔貫直隸松江府上海縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字子崇，行一，年三十二，正月二十八日生〕。曾祖瑾，祖欽，父激，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄繼爵，弟繼俸、繼傑。娶石氏。應天府鄉試第五十一名，會試第一百九十三名。

translation_en:
Jiang Zigao, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zongxiao, he ranked fifteenth in family order, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kui (honorarily appointed Magistrate), his grandfather was Rong (Secretary in the Ministry of Works), his father was Yingqi, and his mother was née Zhu; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Zichu, Zitai, Zilu, Zida, and Zimu, and his younger brothers were Zihe, Zichen, Zishou, and Zizhen; he married a woman née Gong and subsequently a woman née Fang; he ranked forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 310th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Chaofu, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jiezhi, he ranked third in family order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather was Shitai, his father was Hongke, and his mother was née Wu; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Chaobin (Magistrate) and Chaocai (tribute scholar, gongshi), and his younger brothers were Chaocai, Chaojun, Chaoxuan, and Chaoshou; he married a woman née Chen; he ranked sixty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Jilu, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zichong, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather was Qin, his father was Ji, and his mother was née Yang; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Jijue, and his younger brothers were Jifeng and Jijie; he married a woman née Shi; he ranked fifty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Wangdao, registered in Tunliu County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ruzun, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather was Cong (a yin-yang official, responsible for calendrical and divinatory matters), his father was Dongcai, and his mother was née Chen; both parents were living; his younger brother was Zhoudao; he married a woman née Zheng; he ranked first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Dou, registered in a military-officer household of the Yunnan Right Guard in Yunnan and originally from Fengqiu County, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingxiu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Reng was a company commander, granted the honorary title General of Military Strategy; his grandfather Yu was a vice battalion commander, granted the same honorary title; and his father Bin was a battalion commander. His father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Ke, a battalion commander, and Kui, and his wife was née Wang. He placed eleventh in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yike, registered in a military household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhidao, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Gan, his father Da, and his mother née Deng. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Yiben and Yiyuan, and his wife was née Shan. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dang Xu, registered in a bannerman household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and originally from Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Rucheng, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Ping was a company commander, his grandfather was Neng, and his father Huan was a company commander; his legal mother and birth mother were both née Chen. Both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Shou, and his younger brothers were Shen, Huai, vice commander of the Huizhou Guard, and Chao. His wife was née Li. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 362nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jian, registered in a military household in Wei County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Sijin, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng, his grandfather Xing, his father Rui, a National University student, and his mother née Tan. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Qian and Zhuo, and his wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yuan Zurong, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an supplementary student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked second in the family and was aged thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Mengti, a Bureau Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Dashen; his father was Chengxiang, an Unranked Clerk; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zuhua, Zuzhi, Zufang, Zuyi, Zuhui, and Zurui. His wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Ji, registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zichen; he ranked twentieth in the family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Dingxun; his grandfather was Yuqi; his father was Yue; and his mother was née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gang, and his younger brothers were Tong and Yan. His wife was née Zou. He placed eighty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xiluo, registered in a military household of the Taiyuan Left Guard in Shanxi and originally from Jiangdu County in Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zongcheng; he ranked second in the family and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Tang; his father's former wife was née Sheng; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Xilian, a Subprefectural Judge. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Su. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yizheng, registered in a military household in Weinan County, Huazhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Geqing; he ranked first in the family and was aged forty, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather was Jingyang; his father was Jue; and his mother was née Yan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Yizhen, Yicheng, and Yiguan. His wife was née Mou; he subsequently married a woman née Guo. He placed sixty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Tian, courtesy name Ruhuo, was registered in a civilian household in Guangshan County, Guang Prefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Jie, and his father Wenbi; his mother was née Huang. His mother alone was still living. His younger brother was Pu, and his wife was née Dong. He placed twenty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dong, courtesy name Ruzong, was registered in a civilian household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-one, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongquan, a subprefect of a department; his grandfather Hu was granted the title of director of a bureau in the Ministry of War. His father was Tianpeng, and his mother was née Wang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Qu, and his younger brothers were Lai, a student of the National University, Jing, and Wei. His wife was née Gui. He placed eighty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Congjiao, courtesy name Bomian, was registered in a civilian household in Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Gui, and his father Zhi; his mother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Congxun, Conghui, Conghua, and Congshi, and his wife was née Shi. He placed twenty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 341st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Yingfang, courtesy name Weishi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dahong, his grandfather Tingyu, and his father Yuesheng; his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingmei, and his younger brothers were Yingkui, Yinglan, and Yingling. His wife was née Li. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 398th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Wei 何烓, registered in Nanling County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenming, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui, his grandfather Wang, his father Wu, and his mother née Sun; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Mei and Wei, and he married a woman née Wang and subsequently another woman née Wang. He placed 120th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Yaohuan 祝堯煥, registered in Puzhou, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shizheng, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the third day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather An, his father Sigao (an honorary official for longevity), his father's former wife née Wen, and his mother née Jiang; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Yaomin, his younger brothers were Yaochen and Yaoqing, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shuji 馮叔吉, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Rudi, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather's name is transcribed as 兡 [?], his grandfather was He, his father Xie, and his mother née Qian; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Jizhi, Bozhen, and Zhongxiang, his younger brothers were Jizhao and Shaozhan, and he married a woman née Zhou. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Dan 楊旦, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruming, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dechu, his grandfather Ying, his father Quan, and his mother née Xiao; both parents were deceased, his younger brothers were Gen, Min, Sheng 昇, Sheng 晟, and Gao, and he married a woman née Shi and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

熊坦〔貫湖廣武昌府興國州民籍，通山縣人，州學生，治易經，字履道，行一，年四十，五月初九日生〕。曾祖福源，祖朝瓚〔壽官〕，父伯峰〔府通判〕，母吳氏，繼母舒氏。具慶下，弟垣、增、壎。娶謝氏，繼娶易氏。湖廣鄉試第五十四名，會試第三百五十名。

張烈文〔貫雲南蒙化衛軍籍，直隸巢縣人，國子生，治禮記，字元煥，行一，年三十九，七月二十七日生〕。曾祖禮，祖緒，父仲美，母楊氏。嚴侍下，弟烈武、烈光。娶宋氏。雲南鄉試第四名，會試第三百三十九名。

成守節〔貫山東兖州府曹州民籍，山西太谷縣人，國子生，治詩經，字子安，行四，年三十三，十二月初三日生〕。曾祖傑，祖昭，父良卿，母國氏。慈侍下，兄守復〔貢士〕、守業、守恒，弟守身〔貢士〕、守頤、守家、守素、守良。娶張氏。山東鄉試第六十五名，會試第九十九名。
translation_en:
Yi Daotan, courtesy name Jinming, was registered in a civilian household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged forty-two [?; the transcription has 生 in place of the expected 年], and was born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hua, his grandfather Mengke, his father Zi, and his mother née Gong. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Daoyue; his younger brothers were Daolu, Daoxie, Daohe, and Daoyu. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 367th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Tan, courtesy name Lüdao, was registered in a civilian household in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Tongshan County. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Fuyuan; his grandfather Chaozan held an honorary office conferred for longevity; his father Bofeng was an assistant prefect. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Shu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuan, Zeng, and Xun. He married a woman née Xie and subsequently a woman née Yi. He placed fifty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 350th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Liewen, courtesy name Yuanhuan, was registered in a military household in Menghua Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Chao County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Xu, his father Zhongmei, and his mother née Yang. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Liewu and Lieguang. He married a woman née Song. He placed fourth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 339th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shoujie, courtesy name Zi’an, was registered in a civilian household in Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a native of Taigu County, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Zhao, his father Liangqing, and his mother née Guo. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Shoufu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Shouye, and Shouheng; his younger brothers were Shoushen, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Shouyi, Shoujia, Shousu, and Shouliang. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳非玉〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字得瑩，行六，年三十五，三月十八日生〕。曾祖常美〔累贈通議大夫工部左侍郎〕，祖元慶〔累贈通議大夫工部左侍郎〕，父大田〔通議大夫工部左侍郎加正二品服俸〕，母徐氏〔累贈淑人〕，繼母許氏〔累封淑人〕。慈侍下。兄非熊〔官生〕、非羆〔上林苑監典署〕、廣〔貢士〕，弟非璧〔官生〕、非魯。娶陳氏。福建鄉試第六十名，會試第三百九十二名。

translation_en:
Shi Guifang, registered in a civilian household in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingshi; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Chaoda, his grandfather En, and his father Zhongzhao; his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Lianfang and Zaifang, and his wife was née Shen. He placed thirty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Jiong, registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuyuan; he ranked ninth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Shilian, and his father Zai; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Ling. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Chi, a District Magistrate; Tong; Su, a Steward; and Guo, who had been awarded the cap and girdle of official status. His younger brother was Zao. He married a woman née Shu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Feiyu, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Deying; he ranked sixth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather Changmei and grandfather Yuanqing had each received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Works. His father Datian was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Works, additionally granted the robes and salary of rank 2a. His mother, née Xu, had received successive posthumous grants of the title Lady of Virtue; his stepmother, née Xu (許), had received successive grants of the same title. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Feixiong, a student admitted by virtue of an official's privilege; Feipi, an Office Manager in the Directorate of Imperial Parks; and Guang, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Feibi, a student admitted by virtue of an official's privilege, and Feilu. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 392nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ruyan, registered in an officer household of the Wuxiang Left Guard and a native of Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zishen; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the thirtieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Fu and grandfather Hong were both Company Commanders; his father was Lian, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huai, Chao, Xian, Hao, and Han; his younger brother was Ruji. He married a woman née Ma and subsequently a woman née Ni. He placed 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 306th in the Metropolitan Examination.

蕭九成〔貫直隸興州後屯衛軍籍，江西廬陵縣人，三河縣學生，治易經，字汝和，行一，年三十一，十一月二十九日生〕。曾祖昇，祖銳〔府通判〕，父進，母孫氏。永感下，弟九峯〔同知〕、九錫、九思、九敘、九臯、九官，娶沈氏，繼娶韓氏。順天府鄉試第八十七名，會試第一百六十七名。

魏學曾〔貫陝西漢中府金州紫陽縣民籍，直隸涇陽縣人，國子生，治詩經，字惟貫，行二，年二十九，十二月二十日生〕。曾祖禎〔判官〕，祖琫，父守潔，母何氏。慈侍下，兄學顏，弟學思〔監生〕、學孟〔壽官〕、學程、學張，娶任氏，繼娶李氏。陝西鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百二十名。

李得春〔貫湖廣承天府鍾祥縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字茂先，行一，年三十二，四月二十三日生〕。曾祖聰，祖佐，父臯，母錢氏。具慶下，弟應春、近春，娶曹氏。湖廣鄉試第五十八名，會試第三百四十八名。
translation_en:
Xiao Jiucheng, courtesy name Ruhe, was registered in a military household of the Xingzhou Rear Garrison Guard in Zhili and was a native of Luling County, Jiangxi. A student of the Sanhe County school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Rui, was an Assistant Prefect; his father was Jin, and his mother was née Sun. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jiufeng, a Vice Prefect, Jiuxi, Jiusi, Jiuxu, Jiugao, and Jiuguan. He married a woman née Shen and subsequently a woman née Han. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yaozong, courtesy name Jinxian, was registered in a military household of Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shu, who held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather, Yan, was a Department Magistrate; and his father was Bo. His legal mother was née Cui, his stepmothers were née Zhang and née Qin, and his birth mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Linzong. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 349th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Xuezeng, courtesy name Weiguan, was registered in a civilian household of Ziyang County, Jinzhou Department, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Jingyang County, identified here as being in Zhili [?]. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twentieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Zhen, was an Administrative Assistant; his grandfather was Beng; his father was Shoujie, and his mother was née He. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Xueyan; his younger brothers were Xuesi, a student of the Imperial University, Xuemeng, who held an honorary title for longevity, Xuecheng, and Xuezhang. He married a woman née Ren and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dechun, courtesy name Maoxian, was registered in a civilian household of Zhongxiang County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather was Zuo; his father was Gao, and his mother was née Qian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingchun and Jinchun. He married a woman née Cao. He placed fifty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 348th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Tang, registered with the Chengtian Office of Sacrifices in Huguang and a native of Xiangyang County, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rugao, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Min, his father Han, and his mother née Zhao; his mother alone survived, his wife was née Shen, and he placed thirtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ye, of civilian household registration in Gaoling County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weiqin, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zeng, his grandfather Qi, his father Zhongren (a County School Instructor), and his mother née Quan; his parents and grandparents were living, his younger brothers were Pin, Zhuang, Zhi, and Chun, his wife was née Sun, and he placed twenty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 329th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Sijing, of military household registration in the Dezhou Guard, Shandong, and a native of Jiangyin County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Deqin, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Shan, his father Zhao, and his mother née Shen; his mother alone survived, his younger brother was Sizhong, his wife was née Ma, and he placed nineteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pang Shangpeng, of civilian household registration in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shaonan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather’s name is transcribed as 𦶜 [?], his grandfather was Bi, his father Xian, and his mother née Kuang; both parents were living (his elder brothers were Yunyou, Shanggao, Shangzhao, and Shangmo, and his younger brothers were Shangyan, Shangxie, Shangdu, Shangshuo, and Shangwei), his wife was née Yang, and he placed thirty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tian Sanjie, registered in a civilian household in Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zishen; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Wan, his father Yumin, and his mother née Jiao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sanwei and his younger brother Sanxing. His wife was née Song. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Xizai, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Duankui; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Kuan, his father Xiao, and his mother née Qiu. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Yingkui, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenxiu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Jie, and his father Zhang. His father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Xing and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 357th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Youji, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Junqian; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaoshen, posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His grandfather was Liangyong, Grand Master for Fostering Virtue and Minister of Justice at Nanjing, posthumously named Jiansu. His father was Chong'en and his mother née Chen; both were living. His elder brothers were Chongjie, a prefect of a subprefecture; Chonggeng, a prefect; Chongqi; Chong□ [second character illegible]; Youxu; Youtong; Tianzuo; and Youcai. His younger brothers were Youyou, Youyi, Youxun, Youzhen, Youjun, Youyi, and Youquan. His wife was née Lin. He placed seventy-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 359th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Su Zhu, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingfu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty years old, born on the thirtieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shen; his grandfather, Biao; and his father, Chen. His father’s former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Wang. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brother was Rukun, and his wife was née Li. He placed seventy-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Pengxiang, registered in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Xizhou, Shanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yunchong, and he ranked fourth among his brothers. He was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Min, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Qing, an annual tribute student; his father was Ming; and his mother was née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yanling, Pengju, a County Vice Magistrate, and Pengyuan. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Tian. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Lian, registered in Yongfeng County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a county government student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zijun, and he ranked ninth among his brothers. He was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuankui, posthumously appointed a Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Xiang, a Guard Registrar; his father was Mengqi, a Department Magistrate; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qian, Zhan, and Yuan; his younger brothers were Wang, Huan, and Shu. His wife was née Wang. He placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Gang, registered in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to an official household and was originally from Taiping County, Shanxi. He was a department government student and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bolian, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Lun, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Transmission Commissioner at Nanjing; his grandfather was Yingshi, an Assistant Prefect; his father was Gai; and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Huang (𨱑), and his wife was née Meng. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Jie, registered in Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Heqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-four, and was born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Xiong, and his father Xi; his father's former wife was née An, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ce (an honorary official) and Jian. His wife was née Kang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Quan, registered in Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenheng; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanming, his grandfather Hong, and his father Yu; his father's former wife was née Ling, and his mother was née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zhao and his younger brother Jin. His wife was née Ji. He placed eighty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 321st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shunling, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shouqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged fifty-five, and was born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Qi, and his father Qin; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Peiling. His wife was née Xia, and his subsequent wife was née Li. He placed 105th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 338th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yong, registered in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yushi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi (an honorary official), his grandfather Shoushan, and his father Gongji; his mother was née Tong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Jian and Cheng. His wife was née Zhou. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Yan, and his father He; his father’s former wives were née Yan and née Zhao, and his mother was née Huo. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Dayong, Daxian, and Daben, his younger brother was Dabin, and his wife was née Shen. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 351st in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Biao, his grandfather Zhigong, and his father Xi; his legal mother was née Zheng, his stepmother née Bian, and his birth mother née Han. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Kang, Tai, and Sui, and his wife was née Xie. He placed twelfth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Shangru, registered in Jiayu County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jichang, he ranked twelfth in family order, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Nian, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Jing, and his mother was née You. Both parents were living; his younger brother was Shangyou, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Xuan, registered in Qiu County, Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zizhong, he ranked first in family order, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Wenxue, and his father Deyong; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brother was Yao, and his wife was née Yang. He placed fortieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳德駿〔貫湖廣德安府應城縣官籍，國子生，治書經，字房甫，行二，年三十九，正月初八日生〕。曾祖璣，祖鍊〔通判〕，父善〔士〕，母楊氏，繼母趙氏。慈侍下，兄德驥，弟德駰〔貢士〕、德騤、德驤、德騫、德駕，娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第二十一名，會試第三十五名。

古文炳〔貫廣東廣州府番禺縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字仲絖，行一，年四十，二月初九日生〕。曾祖仕賢，祖鍾義，父瑛，母李氏。具慶下，弟文德、文選、文燁，娶汪氏。廣東鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百四十四名。

雷金科〔貫福建建寧府建安縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字公憲，行三十一，年三十四，二月二十一日生〕。曾祖仕蔡，祖文照，父璠，母童氏，繼母吳氏。慈侍下，兄金聲、金章，弟金堂、金和、金相、金書、金麟，娶朱氏，繼娶楊氏、張氏。福建鄉試第三十一名，會試第五十名。
translation_en:
Chen Dejun, registered in an official household in Yingcheng County, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Fangfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine sui, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather, Lian, was an Assistant Prefect; and his father, Shan, was a scholar. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Zhao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Deji; his younger brothers were Deyin, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi), Dekui, Dexiang, Deqian, and Dejia. His wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Weique, registered in a civilian household in Mengcheng County, Shouzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruyi; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty sui, born on the sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Yuhan. His father's former wife was née Feng, and his mother was née Ge. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Weixian, and his wife was née Wu. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Wenbing, registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongkuang; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty sui, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixian, his grandfather Zhongyi, and his father Ying; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wende, Wenxuan, and Wenye, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Jinke, registered in a civilian household in Jian'an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongxian; he ranked thirty-first in the family birth order and was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shicai, his grandfather Wenzhao, and his father Fan. His mother was née Tong, and his stepmother was née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jinsheng and Jinzhang; his younger brothers were Jintang, Jinhe, Jinxiang, Jinshu, and Jinlin. His wife was née Zhu; his subsequent wives were née Yang and née Zhang. He placed thirty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

張守道〔貫陝西西安府涇陽縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字希賢，行一，年四十一，十二月十九日生〕。曾祖勉，祖傑，父綵，母強氏。具慶下，弟宗道、宏道、寄道，娶邢氏，繼娶邢氏。陝西鄉試第二十名，會試第二百五十一名。

荀延庚〔貫四川嘉定州峨眉縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字季壽，行二，年二十二，二月二十五日生〕。曾祖齡，祖祿〔衛知事〕，父勛〔教授〕，嫡母向氏，生母伯氏。慈侍下，兄延嗣，弟延世、延會、延芳，聘童氏。四川鄉試第六名，會試第六十九名。

侯有功〔貫江西饒州府浮梁縣民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字思謙，行五十六，年二十，十月二十一日生〕。曾祖貴，祖崇，父仕，前母李氏、潘氏，母盧氏。具慶下，兄有觀、有能，弟有德、有慶，娶徐氏。江西鄉試第九十名，會試第三百十四名。
translation_en:
Ji Yongkang, courtesy name Keyong, was registered in a banner household of the Cangzhou Defense Battalion in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Tianjin Left Guard. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Cong, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Dao, a Guard Registrar; and his mother was née Liu. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brother was Yongli, and his wife was née Qiu. He placed ninety-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shoudao, courtesy name Xixian, was registered in a military household in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Mian, his grandfather was Jie, his father was Cai, and his mother was née Qiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongdao, Hongdao, and Jidao. His wife was née Xing; he subsequently married another woman née Xing. He placed twentieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xun Yangeng, courtesy name Jishou, was registered in a civilian household in Emei County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. A county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Ling; his grandfather was Lu, a Guard Clerk; and his father was Xun, a Prefectural School Instructor. His legal mother was née Xiang, and his birth mother was née Bo. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Yansi, and his younger brothers were Yanshi, Yanhui, and Yanfang. He was betrothed to a woman née Tong. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Yougong, courtesy name Siqian, was registered in a civilian household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifty-sixth in his family and was aged twenty, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather was Chong, and his father was Shi. His father’s former wives were née Li and née Pan; his mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Youguan and Youneng, and his younger brothers were Youde and Youqing. His wife was née Xu. He placed ninetieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉得寬〔貫山西平陽府解州安邑縣，竈籍，河東運司學生，治詩經，字幼平，行三，年三十八，三月十二日生〕。曾祖藩，祖淮，父栻，母張氏。慈侍下，兄從寬〔貢士〕、惟寬，娶謝氏，繼娶張氏、常氏。山西鄉試第四十五名，會試第四十名。
translation_en:
Huang Xixian, courtesy name Borong, was registered in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Houchang, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Shifang; and his father was Wenkui. His mother was née Zuo, and his stepmothers were née Wang, Li, and Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chen, a county school student, and Xikui; his younger brothers were Xizeng and Ximeng. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yiyang, courtesy name Daoyuan, was registered in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather was Gong; and his father was Zhang. His mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yifu. He married a woman née Zhuang. He ranked thirty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 363rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhi, courtesy name Bendao, was registered in Xinzhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yaochen, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Jukui, a Judge; and his father was Kai. His mother was née Tan. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Hao, Xi, Luo, Zhou, Ting, and Jian. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twelfth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dekuan, courtesy name Youping, was registered in Anyi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, in a salt-producing household. A student of the school of the Hedong Salt Distribution Commission specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fan; his grandfather was Huai; and his father was Shi. His mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Congkuan, a tribute student, and Weikuan. He married a woman née Xie, followed by successive wives née Zhang and Chang. He ranked forty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Tingwei, registered in a civilian household in Yongchuan County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zengfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the thirteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qiong; his grandfather, Zun, was a School Instructor posthumously granted the title of Secretary; and his father, Hongzai, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His legal mother, née Long, was granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Tingji, Tingzhe, Tinghe, and Tingming. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed forty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Kexin, registered in a civilian household in Pingxiang County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Bi, was a County Clerk; his grandfather, Yin, was a County Magistrate; his father, Chongde, was a Prefectural School Professor; and his mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Keren, Keyi, Keshi, and Kejia. He married a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An Qian, registered in a scholar household in Cheng'an County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruguang; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-three years old, born on the third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Xian; his father was Jixun; his mother was née Chang; and his stepmother was née Han. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Xiang and Nuo. He married a woman née Shi and subsequently a woman née Han. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Zhen, registered in a civilian household in Hejiang County, Luzhou, Sichuan, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rudong; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-one years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Haikuan, was granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Fan, was a Guard Registrar; his father, Shijiao, was a tribute student (gongshi); and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xi, Xiao, and Ming; his younger brothers were Yi, Jin, Sheng, Xun, and Cui. He married a woman née Ren. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xie Chaoxi, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Huaibang; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Jinhai, his father Mingzhi, and his mother née Ding. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Chaopin and Chaoxi (朝璽). He married a woman née Jin. He placed thirty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Yong, registered in Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and served as Instructor in the county school of Xiaofeng, Zhejiang. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xingke; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wei, his grandfather Jinghua (holder of an honorary rank for longevity), and his father Yong. His father's former wife was née Zheng, and his mother was née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Yueqian, Yueyan, and Yueqiang. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zongyi, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yingheng; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Maozhi, his grandfather Kongzhao, his father Mengjue, his mother née Chen, and his stepmother née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zongyong and Zongcong, and his younger brothers Zong[?] (宗𫒀) and Zongzhen. He married a woman née Shi and subsequently a woman née Yan. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wenzheng, registered in Wei County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daoxing; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Chen, his father Zuo, and his mother née Jing. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wencui (a tribute student) and Wende, and his younger brothers Wenjiao and Wenzhi. He married a woman née Ding. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ji Ke, registered in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yudeng. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengzong, his grandfather Wenchang, and his father Kui; his father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brother was He, and his wife was née Xing. He placed sixtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Fuchun, registered in Hui'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military salt-producing household and was a National University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jingyan. He ranked first among his brothers and was forty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Duo, and his father Tao; his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Zhuang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shouchun, Huichun (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Changchun, Yuchun, Lichun, and Yingchun. His wife was née Jiang. He placed seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Qi, registered in Yuncheng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingwen. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight, born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai (a department magistrate), his grandfather Xiang, and his father Qing; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jun, Yu, and Jiao; his younger brothers were Bin, Bei, and Xun. His wife was née Liu. He placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jin, registered in Jingxing County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Lifu. He ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-eight, born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen (a district magistrate), his grandfather Xiang, and his father Bangwei; his mother was née Bi. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Xuan, Lian, Hao, and Ying. His wife was née Lü. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

龔情，貫直隸松江府上海縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字善甫，行四，年四十，正月二十七日生。曾祖暉，祖頫，父祐，母葉氏。永感下。兄恒、博、恪，弟愷〔監察御史〕。娶曹氏。應天府鄉試第四十七名，會試第八十二名。

吳過，貫河南汝寧府汝陽縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字撿之，行三，年四十，十二月十五日生。曾祖曇，祖聰，父鉞，母孫氏。永感下。兄違、逸。娶汪氏。河南鄉試第三十名，會試第三百八十七名。

陳瑞，貫福建福州府長樂縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字孔麟，行三，年三十六，八月二十日生。曾祖英，祖垔〔贈監察御史〕，父大倫，母林氏。慈侍下。弟璋、琦、珎。娶林氏。福建鄉試第七十八名，會試第二百八十八名。

霍超，貫廣東廣州府南海縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字叔謙，行一，年三十八，四月二十八日生。曾祖弘，祖從，父綸，母梁氏。慈侍下。弟亘、允升、健、紹升。娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第四十二名，會試第二百七十四名。
translation_en:
Gong Qing 龔情 was registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, under civilian registration, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shanfu. Fourth in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Fu, his father You, and his mother née Ye. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Heng, Bo, and Ke; his younger brother Kai was an Investigating Censor. His wife was née Cao. He placed forty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Guo 吳過 was registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, under civilian registration, and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jianzhi. Third in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tan, his grandfather Cong, his father Yue, and his mother née Sun. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wei and Yi. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 387th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Rui 陳瑞 was registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, under military registration, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Konglin. Third in birth order, he was thirty-six years old and was born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather Yin was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His father was Dalun, and his mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Zhang, Qi, and Zhen. His wife was née Lin. He placed seventy-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huo Chao 霍超 was registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, under civilian registration, and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shuqian. First in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Cong, his father Lun, and his mother née Liang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Gen, Yunsheng, Jian, and Shaosheng. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Nian, registered in Jianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Kefu, and he ranked third in family order. He was forty-three years old, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Xun, was a National University student; and his father, Yi, was an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Yang, his mother née Qian, and his stepmother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were He and Qian, and his wife was née Chen. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Dong, registered in Jimo County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kongcai, and he ranked fourth in family order. He was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Zi, was an Assistant Magistrate; his grandfather was Xiren, his father Zhi, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gui, Chun, and Hui, and his wife was née Lan. He placed forty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Fu, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a National University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zizhen, and he ranked third in family order. He was forty years old, born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhaosheng, his grandfather Bodao, and his father Hao; his mother and stepmother were both née Wan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mingyang, a Clerk, and Dongyang; his younger brothers were Gaoyang, Luoyang, Kongyang, and Qianyang. His wife was née Wei. He placed ninety-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Wenmao, registered in Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shifu, and he ranked sixty-third in family order. He was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Lang, his grandfather Xiu, and his father Xu; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Zhu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Wensheng and Wenji, and his wife was née Tian. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.
